dataPoints.label: Women's share of gross annual pay
dataPoints.population: All staff on the unit's own payroll
dataPoints.payElement: Annual total cash pay actually paid
dataPoints.definition: Gross wages paid to women divided by gross wages paid to all staff. This is S itself (BRSR P5 EI-3(b); BRSR Core Attribute 6). The ISF wage definition (salaries, bonuses and other compensation, excluding retirement benefits and ESOPs) rests on a secondary summary and is unverified. Wages of contract labour paid through contractors usually sit outside the bill.

dataPoints.label: Total annual pay paid to women
dataPoints.definition: Sum of gross pay paid to women in the year, all pay elements. Italy Art. 46 total remuneration by sex; Belgium social balance sheet personnel costs by gender; summable from employee-level files (Illinois pay data, confidential).

dataPoints.label: Total annual pay paid to men
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of pay.all.total.annual.women.

dataPoints.label: Total annual pay bill
dataPoints.definition: Gross pay to all staff in the year (the wage bill); Nivel's payroll weight. Inputs to BRSR Core; employee benefits expense in the accounts; Japan's yuho gives average annual salary and employees for the filer only.

dataPoints.label: Women's mean hourly pay
dataPoints.payElement: Gross hourly pay, ordinary plus variable
dataPoints.definition: Mean of women's gross pay per hour paid. Input to the hourly gap; California's pay data report gives it per job category, race and sex cell (W-2 pay over hours; confidential).

dataPoints.label: Men's mean hourly pay
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of pay.all.mean.hourly.women.

dataPoints.label: Women's median hourly pay
dataPoints.definition: Median of women's gross hourly pay. California gives it per cell (confidential).

dataPoints.label: Men's median hourly pay
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of pay.all.median.hourly.women.

dataPoints.label: Women's mean annual pay
dataPoints.definition: Women's total annual pay divided by the number of women, using average headcount over the year. Japan WAA computes it (total wages over average monthly headcount) but publishes only the ratio; Spain EINF average remuneration by sex (company-defined pay) and the pay register; Illinois average compensation (confidential).

dataPoints.label: Men's mean annual pay
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of pay.all.mean.annual.women.

dataPoints.label: Women's median annual pay
dataPoints.definition: Median of women's annual pay. BRSR P5 EI-3(a) gives it only by category (employees other than board and KMP; workers), with the number of women, on a mixed pay concept; Spain's pay register by sex.

dataPoints.label: Men's median annual pay
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of pay.all.median.annual.women.

dataPoints.label: Women's mean full-time-equivalent pay
dataPoints.definition: Mean of women's total remuneration grossed up to full-time hours and a full year. WGEA collects it employee by employee and publishes only gaps; Spain's register tool gives full-time values (unverified).

dataPoints.label: Men's mean full-time-equivalent pay

dataPoints.label: Men's median full-time-equivalent pay

dataPoints.label: Men's mean annual base salary
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of pay.all.mean.annual-base.women.

dataPoints.label: Women's mean full-time-equivalent base salary
dataPoints.definition: Mean of women's base salary annualised to full-time, full-year (WGEA input).

dataPoints.label: Men's mean full-time-equivalent base salary
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of pay.all.mean.fte-base.women.

dataPoints.label: Women's median full-time-equivalent base salary
dataPoints.definition: Median of women's annualised FTE base salary (WGEA input).

dataPoints.label: Men's median full-time-equivalent base salary
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of pay.all.median.fte-base.women.

dataPoints.label: Average annual pay, all staff

dataPoints.label: Average full-time-equivalent pay, all staff
dataPoints.definition: Average annualised FTE total remuneration of the whole workforce, not by gender (WGEA employer gaps file).

dataPoints.label: Mean hourly pay gap
dataPoints.payElement: Gross hourly pay, ordinary plus variable
dataPoints.period: Reporting year; a snapshot pay period is approximate
dataPoints.definition: (Men's mean hourly pay minus women's) over men's; positive means women are paid less; W = 1 minus it. UK Reg 2(1)(a): full-pay relevant employees of each legal employer, ordinary pay plus bonus pro-rated to the pay period containing 5 April (31 March public). ESRS 2023 S1-16 s97(a) and ESRS 2026 S1-15 s40(a): all employees, gross hourly, base plus variable. PTD Art. 9(1)(a) hourly form; SFDR PAI 12; Scotland excludes overtime. Category or country splits are qualifiers.

dataPoints.label: Median hourly pay gap
dataPoints.definition: (Men's median hourly pay minus women's) over men's. UK Reg 2(1)(b); PTD Art. 9(1)(c) hourly form; voluntary under ESRS.

dataPoints.label: Mean annual pay gap
dataPoints.definition: 1 minus women's mean annual total pay per head as a share of men's. Japan WAA publishes the ratio (women's mean annual wage per 100 of men's; total wages over average monthly headcount; retirement and commuting allowances may be excluded); gap = 1 minus ratio. PTD Art. 9(1)(a) annual form; Spain EINF brecha salarial (company method). A disclosed ratio and gap on one basis share this atom.
globalItems: GRI 405-2-a ratio of remuneration, women to men

dataPoints.label: Median annual pay gap

dataPoints.label: Mean full-time-equivalent pay gap
dataPoints.definition: (Men's mean annualised FTE total remuneration minus women's) over men's. WGEA average total remuneration gap: Australian employees including the CEO from 2023-24 data; excludes non-binary, zero-income and overseas reporting managers; total = base plus super, bonuses, overtime, allowances and incentives.

dataPoints.label: Median full-time-equivalent pay gap
dataPoints.definition: (Men's median annualised FTE total remuneration minus women's) over men's. WGEA's headline; target range -5% to +5%.

dataPoints.label: Median full-time-equivalent base salary gap
dataPoints.definition: Median gap on annualised FTE base salary (WGEA).

dataPoints.label: Mean base salary gap
dataPoints.definition: 1 minus women's mean base salary as a share of men's. GRI 405-2-a basic salary ratio (per category and significant location; time unit and average not fixed); PTD Art. 9(1)(g) basic pay by category; Spain's register. Category and location are qualifiers.

dataPoints.label: Adjusted pay gap or ratio (company model)

dataPoints.definition: A gap or ratio controlling for role, level, location or tenure, on the company's own model (common in US filings; Bloomberg GEI Q28). Does not give W.

dataPoints.label: Median bonus gap
dataPoints.definition: Median variant among recipients (UK Reg 2(1)(d); PTD Art. 9(1)(d) where recipients only).

dataPoints.label: Mean variable pay gap per worker

dataPoints.definition: Median variant counting all workers (PTD Art. 9(1)(d) reading); not computable from the recipients' median.

dataPoints.label: Share of men receiving a bonus

globalItems: SASB TC-SI-330a.3, FN-AC-330a.1, FN-IB-330a.1, SV-PS-330a.1 (executive management)

dataPoints.label: Women in top management
dataPoints.population: Two management levels below the board
dataPoints.definition: Women in the two levels below the board: ESRS top management (one and two levels below the administrative bodies, or the company's own definition); UK executive committee plus direct reports; Netherlands subtop.

dataPoints.label: Men in top management
dataPoints.population: Two management levels below the board
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of headcount.topmgmt.count.women.

dataPoints.label: Women's share of top management
dataPoints.population: Two management levels below the board
dataPoints.definition: Share form of headcount.topmgmt.count.women (ESRS S1-9 s66(a), S1-8 s26(a); UK women in leadership).

dataPoints.label: Women senior managers
dataPoints.definition: Women responsible for planning, directing or controlling the company or a strategically significant part (UK s414C(8)(c)(ii), including subsidiary directors in groups); US EEO-1 Executive/Senior Level Officials and Managers.

dataPoints.label: Men senior managers
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of headcount.senior-managers.count.women.

dataPoints.label: Women's share of senior management
dataPoints.definition: Share form of headcount.senior-managers.count.women. France cadres dirigeants (Rixain) map here approximately.

dataPoints.label: Women managers
dataPoints.definition: Women in all management roles: Japan section manager (kacho) level and above excluding officers; WGEA managers (CEO, KMP, other executives, senior and other managers; manager category is a qualifier); US EEO-1 two management categories.

dataPoints.label: Men managers
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of headcount.managers.count.women.

dataPoints.label: Women's share of managers
dataPoints.definition: Share form of headcount.managers.count.women; mandatory in Japan for 101 or more workers from April 2026.

dataPoints.label: Women's share of supervisors (Japan)
dataPoints.definition: Women at assistant-manager level, one rung below section manager (WAA optional item).

dataPoints.label: Women non-managers
dataPoints.definition: Women employees who are not managers (WGEA; occupation is a qualifier).

dataPoints.label: Men non-managers
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of headcount.nonmanagers.count.women.

dataPoints.label: Women's share of non-managers
dataPoints.definition: Share form of headcount.nonmanagers.count.women.

dataPoints.label: Women among the ten highest paid
dataPoints.definition: Women among the ten highest earners; France Index Indicator 5 counts the under-represented sex.

dataPoints.label: Women hired
dataPoints.definition: Women who joined as new employees in the year (GRI 401-1-a; WGEA appointments; Italy Art. 46).
globalItems: WEF SCM core: Employment and wealth generation

dataPoints.label: Men hired
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of flows.all.count.hires.women.

dataPoints.label: Women's share of hires
dataPoints.definition: Women over all hires (WEPs; Japan WAA optional item; Bloomberg Q16).

dataPoints.label: Hire rate, women
dataPoints.definition: Women hired over women employed at period end (GRI 401-1-a recommendation).

dataPoints.label: Hire rate, men
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of flows.all.rate.hires.women.

dataPoints.label: Women who left
dataPoints.definition: Women who left for any reason: resignation, dismissal, retirement or death (GRI 401-1-b).

dataPoints.label: Men who left
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of flows.all.count.leavers.women.

dataPoints.label: Employees who left
dataPoints.definition: All leavers, not by gender (ESRS 2023 S1-6 s50(c)).

dataPoints.label: Turnover rate, women
dataPoints.definition: Women leavers over women employed (GRI uses period-end headcount; Bloomberg Q15 attrition).

dataPoints.label: Turnover rate, men
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of flows.all.rate.leavers.women.

dataPoints.label: Turnover rate
dataPoints.definition: Leavers over employees, not by gender (ESRS 2023 s50(c); ESRS 2026 S1-5 s19(c)).

dataPoints.label: Turnover rate, permanent women (India)
dataPoints.definition: Permanent women who left (any reason) x 100 over the average of opening and closing permanent women; employees and workers as separate rows; three-year trend (BRSR A-22).

dataPoints.label: Turnover rate, permanent men (India)
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of flows.permanent.rate.leavers.women.

dataPoints.label: Women who resigned
dataPoints.definition: Voluntary exits by women (WGEA resignations, by status and manager type).

dataPoints.label: Men who resigned
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of flows.all.count.resignations.women.

dataPoints.label: Resignation rate, women
dataPoints.definition: Women's resignations over women employed (WGEA proportion).

dataPoints.label: Resignation rate, men
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of flows.all.rate.resignations.women.

dataPoints.label: Women dismissed
dataPoints.definition: Dismissals of women (Spain EINF).

dataPoints.label: Men dismissed
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of flows.all.count.dismissals.women.

dataPoints.label: Women promoted
dataPoints.definition: Women moved to a higher level or grade in the year (WGEA; Italy Art. 46; Bloomberg Q14).

dataPoints.label: Men promoted
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of flows.all.count.promotions.women.

dataPoints.label: Women's share of promotions
dataPoints.definition: Women over all promotions.

dataPoints.label: Promotion rate, women
dataPoints.definition: Women promoted over women employed (France Index Indicator 3 by job category; WGEA).

dataPoints.label: Promotion rate, men
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of flows.all.rate.promotions.women.

dataPoints.label: Women promoted into management
dataPoints.definition: Women promoted from non-manager to manager (WGEA).

dataPoints.label: Men promoted into management
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of flows.nonmanagers.count.promotions-to-manager.women.

dataPoints.label: Women appointed to management roles
dataPoints.definition: Women appointed to manager roles, internally or externally, by manager type (WGEA).

dataPoints.label: Men appointed to management roles
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of flows.managers.count.appointments.women.

dataPoints.label: Share of women given a pay rise
dataPoints.definition: Women receiving an individual raise over all women (France Index Indicator 2; by job category, excluding promotions, above 250 staff).

dataPoints.label: Share of men given a pay rise
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of flows.all.rate.raises.women.

dataPoints.label: Women moved to regular or permanent contracts
dataPoints.definition: Women converted between employment types, such as non-regular to regular (Japan WAA optional item; Italy transitions).

dataPoints.label: Men moved to regular or permanent contracts
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of flows.all.count.conversions.women.

dataPoints.label: Women hired mid-career (Japan)
dataPoints.definition: Women hired mid-career (WAA optional item).

dataPoints.label: Men hired mid-career (Japan)
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of flows.all.count.midcareer-hires.women.

dataPoints.label: Women rehired (Japan)
dataPoints.definition: Women rehired after leaving (WAA optional item).

dataPoints.label: Men rehired (Japan)
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of flows.all.count.rehires.women.

dataPoints.label: Applicants per hire, women (Japan)
dataPoints.definition: Women applicants over women hired (WAA item, dropped from the MHLW database in January 2025; history only).

dataPoints.label: Applicants per hire, men (Japan)
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of flows.all.ratio.applicants-per-hire.women.

dataPoints.label: Women still employed about 10 years after hire
dataPoints.definition: Share of women hired about ten years earlier who are still employed (WAA optional item).

dataPoints.label: Men still employed about 10 years after hire
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of flows.hire-cohort.rate.retention-10y.women.

dataPoints.label: Women's average length of service
dataPoints.definition: Average continuous years of service of women on indefinite-term contracts (WAA optional item).

dataPoints.label: Men's average length of service
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of tenure.permanent.mean.years.women.

dataPoints.label: Gap in average length of service
dataPoints.definition: Men's average service minus women's, or the ratio as published (WAA optional item).

dataPoints.label: Women entitled to parental leave
dataPoints.definition: Women entitled to parental leave under policy or law (GRI 401-3-a).

dataPoints.label: Men entitled to parental leave
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of leave.all.count.entitled.women.

dataPoints.label: Share of staff entitled to family leave
dataPoints.definition: Employees entitled to family-related leave over all employees, not by gender (ESRS 2023 S1-15 s93(a); ESRS 2026 S1-14 s38).

dataPoints.label: Women who took parental leave
dataPoints.definition: Women who took parental or carer's leave; leave type (parental, primary or secondary carer, employer-funded) is a qualifier (GRI 401-3-b; WGEA).

dataPoints.label: Men who took parental leave
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of leave.all.count.taken.women.

dataPoints.label: Family leave uptake, women
dataPoints.definition: Entitled women who took family-related leave over entitled women (ESRS 2023 S1-15 s93(b)).

dataPoints.label: Family leave uptake, men
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of leave.entitled.rate.taken.women.

dataPoints.label: Childcare leave uptake, women (Japan)
dataPoints.population: Women who gave birth in the year
dataPoints.definition: Women taking statutory childcare leave over women who gave birth (WAA optional item, by employment category).

dataPoints.label: Childcare leave uptake, men (Japan)
dataPoints.population: Men whose spouse gave birth in the year
dataPoints.definition: Men taking childcare leave over men whose spouse gave birth; can exceed 100%. WAA counts statutory leave only; CCLA option (i) also counts equivalent employer measures (approximate). Mandatory above 300 workers; in the yuho.

dataPoints.label: Childcare and childcare-purpose leave uptake, men (Japan)
dataPoints.population: Men whose spouse gave birth in the year
dataPoints.definition: CCLA option (ii): as option (i) plus employer childcare-purpose leave for children below school age. The company states which option.

dataPoints.label: Women who returned from parental leave
dataPoints.definition: Women who returned in the period after leave ended (GRI 401-3-c).

dataPoints.label: Men who returned from parental leave
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of leave.all.count.returned.women.

dataPoints.label: Return-to-work rate, women
dataPoints.definition: Women who returned over women due to return (GRI 401-3-e).

dataPoints.label: Return-to-work rate, men
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of leave.all.rate.return.women.

dataPoints.label: Women still employed 12 months after return
dataPoints.definition: Women still employed 12 months after returning (GRI 401-3-d).

dataPoints.label: Men still employed 12 months after return
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of leave.all.count.retained-12m.women.

dataPoints.label: Retention after parental leave, women
dataPoints.definition: Women retained 12 months after return over women who returned in the prior period (GRI 401-3-e; WEPs uses FTE).

dataPoints.label: Retention after parental leave, men
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of leave.all.rate.retention-12m.women.

dataPoints.label: Return-to-work rate, permanent women (India)
dataPoints.definition: As leave.all.rate.return.women for permanent employees and workers, maternity and paternity leave (BRSR P3 EI-5).

dataPoints.label: Return-to-work rate, permanent men (India)
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of leave.permanent.rate.return.women.

dataPoints.label: Retention after parental leave, permanent women (India)
dataPoints.definition: As leave.all.rate.retention-12m.women for permanent staff (BRSR P3 EI-5).

dataPoints.label: Retention after parental leave, permanent men (India)
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of leave.permanent.rate.retention-12m.women.

dataPoints.label: Women who left during parental leave
dataPoints.definition: Women whose employment ended while on paid parental leave (WGEA).

dataPoints.label: Men who left during parental leave
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of leave.all.count.left-during-leave.women.

dataPoints.label: Women given the catch-up raise after maternity leave
dataPoints.population: Women returning from maternity or adoption leave
dataPoints.definition: Share of returners given the legally required catch-up raise (France Index Indicator 4).

dataPoints.label: Weeks of employer-paid parental leave
dataPoints.definition: Weeks of employer-funded paid parental leave, primary or secondary carer as a qualifier (WGEA Q4.1; Equileap criterion 8, paid at two-thirds or more; GRI 107 days beyond the legal minimum, draft).

dataPoints.label: Health insurance coverage, women
dataPoints.definition: Women covered by health insurance over all women, by permanence and category (BRSR P3 EI-1).

dataPoints.label: Health insurance coverage, men
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of benefits.all.rate.health-insurance.women.

dataPoints.label: Accident insurance coverage, women
dataPoints.definition: As benefits.all.rate.health-insurance.women for accident insurance.

dataPoints.label: Accident insurance coverage, men
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of benefits.all.rate.accident-insurance.women.

dataPoints.label: Maternity benefit coverage, women
dataPoints.definition: As benefits.all.rate.health-insurance.women for maternity benefits.

dataPoints.label: Maternity benefit coverage, men
dataPoints.definition: Men's row of the BRSR maternity benefit item.

dataPoints.label: Paternity benefit coverage, women
dataPoints.definition: Women's row of the BRSR paternity benefit item.

dataPoints.label: Paternity benefit coverage, men
dataPoints.definition: As benefits.all.rate.health-insurance.women for paternity benefits, men.

dataPoints.label: Day-care coverage, women
dataPoints.definition: As benefits.all.rate.health-insurance.women for day-care facilities.

dataPoints.label: Day-care coverage, men
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of benefits.all.rate.day-care.women.

dataPoints.label: Average training hours, women
dataPoints.definition: Total training hours of women over women employees (GRI 404-1; ESRS 2023 S1-13 s83(b); ESRS 2026 drops the gender split).

dataPoints.label: Average training hours, men
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of training.all.mean.hours.women.

dataPoints.label: Women trained in health and safety
dataPoints.definition: Women given health and safety training over all women; employees and workers as qualifiers (BRSR P3 EI-8).

dataPoints.label: Men trained in health and safety
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of training.all.rate.health-safety.women.

dataPoints.label: Women given skills training
dataPoints.definition: Women given skill-upgradation training over all women (BRSR P3 EI-8; historic BRR for permanent women).

dataPoints.label: Men given skills training
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of training.all.rate.skills.women.

dataPoints.label: Performance reviews, women
dataPoints.definition: Women who had a regular performance and career review over all women (GRI 404-3; ESRS 2023 s83(a); BRSR P3 EI-9).

dataPoints.label: Performance reviews, men
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of training.all.rate.reviews.women.

dataPoints.label: Anti-harassment workshops held
dataPoints.definition: Workshops or awareness programmes against sexual harassment (POSH Rules, rule 14(d)).

dataPoints.label: Sexual harassment complaints
dataPoints.period: Financial year (POSH committee report: calendar year)
dataPoints.definition: Sexual harassment complaints filed or received in the year (BRSR P5 EI-6 and EI-7; Companies (Accounts) Rules 8(5)(x)(a); POSH Act s22).

dataPoints.label: Sexual harassment complaints pending at year end
dataPoints.definition: Complaints pending resolution at year end (BRSR P5 EI-6).

dataPoints.label: Sexual harassment cases pending over 90 days
dataPoints.definition: Cases pending more than ninety days (rule 8(5)(x)(c); POSH rule 14(c)).

dataPoints.label: Sexual harassment complaints disposed of
dataPoints.definition: Complaints disposed of in the year (rule 8(5)(x)(b); POSH rule 14(b)).

dataPoints.label: Sexual harassment complaints upheld
dataPoints.definition: POSH complaints upheld (BRSR P5 EI-7; BRSR Core Attribute 6).

dataPoints.label: Sexual harassment complaints per women employed
dataPoints.definition: POSH complaints as a % of female employees and workers (BRSR P5 EI-7; ISF denominator text not retrieved).

dataPoints.label: Discrimination complaints or incidents
dataPoints.definition: Discrimination at work in the year, all grounds including sex, not split by gender (BRSR P5 EI-6 complaints; GRI 406-1 incidents; ESRS 2026 S1-16 s42(a)).

dataPoints.label: Discrimination complaints pending at year end
dataPoints.definition: Discrimination complaints pending at year end (BRSR P5 EI-6).

dataPoints.label: Discrimination incidents including harassment
dataPoints.definition: Incidents of discrimination including harassment reported in the period (ESRS 2023 S1-17 s103(a)).

dataPoints.label: Action taken on complaints
dataPoints.definition: Nature of action taken (POSH rule 14(e)); status of incidents and remediation (GRI 406-1).

dataPoints.label: Equal pay policy
dataPoints.definition: Whether an equal remuneration policy or strategy exists (WGEA GEI 3; WEPs Tool). India's Code on Wages and the repealed 1976 Act are legal duties with no disclosure.

dataPoints.label: Pay gap analysis done
dataPoints.definition: Whether, and when, a gender pay analysis or audit was done (WGEA s8(1)(c); Bloomberg Q27; Spain's pay audit).

dataPoints.label: Joint pay assessment triggered
dataPoints.definition: Whether a category gap of 5% or more, unexplained and not fixed in six months, triggered a joint pay assessment (PTD Art. 10).

dataPoints.label: 25% pay difference justified (Spain)
dataPoints.definition: Whether the pay register carries the justification required when one sex's average pay is 25% or more above the other's (ET art. 28.3).

dataPoints.label: Equality or action plan in place
dataPoints.definition: Whether a gender equality or action plan exists (Spain plan; Japan WAA action plan; France corrective measures below 75 points; UK equality action plans; Northern Ireland proposal).

dataPoints.label: Actions in the plan
dataPoints.definition: The actions chosen, with timing (UK: at least one pay gap action and one menopause action from the government list; Japan plan targets and actions; WGEA actions after gap analysis).

dataPoints.label: Board diversity policy
dataPoints.definition: Board diversity policy and how diversity is considered in nominations and succession (UK DTR 7.2.8AR; US S-K 407(c)(2)(vi); Washington discussion and analysis; Japan Code Principle 4-13(1) and skills matrix; WGEA GEI 2 policy).

dataPoints.label: Workforce diversity policy
dataPoints.definition: Diversity and inclusion policy, initiatives and progress (ASX Rec 1.5(a); UK Code Provision 23; Japan human capital policy; US human capital description).

dataPoints.label: Flexible work policy
dataPoints.definition: Flexible working arrangements available (WGEA GEI 4).

dataPoints.label: Carer support policy
dataPoints.definition: Support for employees with family or caring responsibilities (WGEA GEI 4; GRI 107 draft).

dataPoints.label: Family and domestic violence support
dataPoints.definition: Family and domestic violence support or leave (WGEA s9(n) to (o)).

dataPoints.label: Harassment prevention policy and process
dataPoints.definition: Policy, training and complaint process for sexual harassment and discrimination, and whether complaint data is collected (WGEA GEI 6; India internal committee statement; WEPs grievance mechanism).

dataPoints.label: Employee consultation on gender equality
dataPoints.definition: Whether, how and with whom employees were consulted (WGEA GEI 5).

dataPoints.label: Maternity Benefit Act compliance statement
dataPoints.definition: Board report statement of compliance with the Maternity Benefit Act 1961 (rule 8(5)(xiii)).

dataPoints.label: Pay range shown in job postings
dataPoints.definition: Whether postings show a good-faith pay range (US state laws). Not gender-specific; a transparency condition.

dataPoints.label: Pay records kept
dataPoints.definition: Job title and wage rate history kept (California 432.3); wage registers (India). Not published.

dataPoints.label: Outsourcing providers named
dataPoints.definition: Providers of outsourced or contract workers outside the relevant-employee count (UK ERA 2025, not in force).

dataPoints.label: Supporting narrative
dataPoints.definition: Explanation of the figures and a link to the employer's own report (UK GPG; WGEA employer statements; Japan notes; Scotland equal pay statement).

dataPoints.label: Target share of women on the board
dataPoints.definition: The company's own target for women's share of board seats; target year and baseline on the observation (WGEA GEI 2 and s11; ASX measurable objectives; Germany s111(5); Netherlands targets).

dataPoints.label: Target share of women officers (Japan)
dataPoints.definition: Company target or TSE goal (one woman by about 2025; 30% by 2030) for women officers.

dataPoints.label: Target share of women executives
dataPoints.definition: Target for women among executive directors or senior executives (WoB Art. 5(2); Germany Vorstand target; ASX).

dataPoints.label: Target share of women in top management
dataPoints.population: Two management levels below the board
dataPoints.definition: Targets for the two levels below the board (Germany s76(4)); subtop (Netherlands); UK review 40% leadership aim.

dataPoints.label: Target share of women managers
dataPoints.definition: Target for women in management (Japan action plans and core human resource targets; WGEA s8).

dataPoints.label: Target share of women in the workforce
dataPoints.definition: Workforce gender objective (ASX Rec 1.5(b)).

dataPoints.label: Target for the under-represented gender among non-managers
dataPoints.definition: WGEA s7 numeric target; the under-represented gender may be men.

dataPoints.label: Target for promotions into management
dataPoints.definition: WGEA s9 numeric target for the under-represented gender.

dataPoints.label: Target for a pay quartile
dataPoints.definition: WGEA s10 numeric target for the under-represented gender in a chosen quartile.

dataPoints.label: Target reduction in the pay gap
dataPoints.definition: Nominated reduction in one chosen gap (WGEA s12: mean or median, base or total, FTE); Japan action plans.

dataPoints.label: Target reduction in managers' pay gap
dataPoints.definition: WGEA s13 target on managers' total remuneration gap, mean or median.

dataPoints.label: Target reduction in non-managers' pay gap
dataPoints.definition: WGEA s13 target for non-managers.

dataPoints.label: Target for men's parental leave uptake
dataPoints.definition: Target uptake of parental or childcare leave by men or the under-represented gender (WGEA s17; Japan Next-Generation Act plans).

dataPoints.label: Other selected targets
dataPoints.definition: Other numeric or action targets chosen from a menu (WGEA ss14 to 25, three per cycle with one numeric), with baseline and value.

dataPoints.label: Target outcome
dataPoints.definition: Met, improved or not met against baseline, with reasons if missed (WGE Act s17C; Germany; ASX progress; WoB and Netherlands reasons).

dataPoints.label: Board meets the gender rule
dataPoints.definition: Whether the board meets its regime's quota or comply-or-explain target, as stated (UK 40%; WoB 40% or 33%; Spain 40%; France 40%; Italy two-fifths; Netherlands one-third; Germany 30%; India one woman and one independent woman; Washington 25%; California and Nasdaq historic). Recomputable from seat counts.

dataPoints.label: A woman holds a senior board role
dataPoints.population: Chair, CEO, senior independent director and CFO
dataPoints.definition: UKLR 6.6.6R(9)(a)(ii) statement.

dataPoints.label: Executives meet the gender rule
dataPoints.definition: France Rixain 30% from 2026 and 40% from 2029; Spain 40% senior management, comply or explain; Germany one woman on a Vorstand above three; WoB executive objectives.

dataPoints.label: Assurance level of gender figures
dataPoints.definition: None, third-party assessment, limited or reasonable assurance over the gender figures (CSRD limited assurance; BRSR Core assessment or assurance; Spain mandatory verification; voluntary ISAE 3000).

dataPoints.label: Assurance provider
dataPoints.definition: Name of the assurer or assessor (BRSR Section A Q14 to 15).

dataPoints.label: Gender figures covered by assurance
dataPoints.definition: Which gender data points the assurance covers (for example BRSR Core Attribute 6: wage share and POSH complaints).

dataPoints.label: Signed statement of accuracy
dataPoints.definition: Figures attested by a named senior person (UK written statement; UK responsible person; WGEA CEO sign-off; Illinois officer certification).

dataPoints.label: How gender is recorded
dataPoints.definition: Sex or gender identity, self-identified or not, and the categories offered (UK biological sex from 21 May 2026 guidance; UK FCA company's choice; US federal forms binary; WGEA non-binary excluded from gaps; ESRS other and not reported).

dataPoints.label: Headcount method
dataPoints.definition: Headcount or FTE, and period end or average (GRI 2-7-c; ESRS s50(d); GRI 105-5-d-ii).

dataPoints.label: Pay method
dataPoints.definition: Mean or median, pay elements included and excluded, and part-time treatment (GRI 105-5-d-i; ESRS AR 34; Japan allowance exclusions; WGEA definitions).

dataPoints.label: Reporting scope
dataPoints.definition: Entity, national arm or group, and locations covered (Japan single entity or group; BRSR standalone or consolidated; GRI significant locations).

dataPoints.label: Share of staff covered by pay data
dataPoints.definition: Share of the workforce whose pay is in the figure (Bloomberg Q29a); Nivel plays only figures covering 90% of payroll.

dataPoints.label: France equality index score
dataPoints.definition: Sum of Index indicator points, prorated if some cannot be calculated; not calculable below 75 achievable points.

dataPoints.label: WEPs gap analysis score
dataPoints.definition: Self-assessment score by area; practice maturity, not payroll data.

dataPoints.label: National mean hourly earnings, women
dataPoints.population: All employees in the national economy
dataPoints.definition: SDG 8.5.1 mean hourly earnings of women (hours-weighted where worker hours exist).

dataPoints.label: National mean hourly earnings, men
dataPoints.population: All employees in the national economy
dataPoints.definition: Men's counterpart of pay.economy.mean.hourly.women.

dataPoints.label: National mean hourly pay gap
dataPoints.population: All employees in the national economy
dataPoints.definition: (Men's minus women's mean hourly earnings) over men's (SDG 8.5.1; ILO).

dataPoints.label: National median hourly pay gap
dataPoints.population: All employees in the national economy
dataPoints.definition: ILO median hourly variant.

dataPoints.label: National mean monthly pay gap
dataPoints.population: All employees in the national economy
dataPoints.definition: ILO mean monthly variant.

dataPoints.label: National median monthly pay gap
dataPoints.population: All employees in the national economy
dataPoints.definition: ILO median monthly variant.

dataPoints.label: National factor-weighted pay gap
dataPoints.population: All employees in the national economy
dataPoints.definition: ILO gap computed within subgroups (education, age, working time, sector) and weighted by size; not a regression-adjusted gap.

dataPoints.label: OECD gender wage gap
dataPoints.population: Full-time employees in the national economy
dataPoints.payElement: Gross weekly or monthly full-time earnings
dataPoints.definition: Difference between men's and women's median full-time earnings over men's (OECD; basis unverified).

dataPoints.label: National share of women in management
dataPoints.definition: SDG 5.5.2 total management, including junior management.

dataPoints.label: National share of women in senior and middle management
dataPoints.population: Employed persons in ISCO-08 groups 11 to 13
dataPoints.definition: SDG 5.5.2 senior and middle management, excluding junior management.

dataPoints.label: Ethnicity pay gap (UK, proposed)
dataPoints.definition: Mean hourly gap between White and all other ethnic groups; the draft bill uses the same six measures as the gender gap.

dataPoints.label: Disability pay gap (UK, proposed)
dataPoints.definition: Mean hourly gap between disabled and non-disabled employees, same six measures.

dataPoints.label: Directors from a minority ethnic background
dataPoints.definition: UKLR 6.6.6R(9)(a)(iii) target of at least one; not a gender measure.

measures.name: Women's share of pay
measures.definition: Women's share of the pay bill, Nivel's headline (parity 50%). Exact: reported totals, or a mean on annual total pay over all staff. Approximate: hourly or FTE inputs, or E and W on different or partial staff. Not computable: median-only or adjusted gaps.
measures.formula: Route 1, reported (India): pay.all.share.annual.women. Route 2, totals: pay.all.total.annual.women / (pay.all.total.annual.women + pay.all.total.annual.men). Route 3, from E and W: E*W / (E*W + 1 - E), E from m.e, W from m.w; exact when W = 1 - pay.all.gap.annual.mean (or pay.all.mean.annual.women / pay.all.mean.annual.men) and E = headcount.all.average.women / (headcount.all.average.women + headcount.all.average.men) on the same staff, since S then equals women's pay over all pay; approximate with pay.all.gap.hourly.mean (UK, EU), pay.all.gap.fte.mean (Australia) or pay.regular.gap.annual.mean, or with E from headcount.all.count.*, headcount.all.share.women, headcount.permanent.share.women, headcount.regular.share.women or the mean of headcount.quartile.share.hourly.women. Route 4, approximate: sum over bands q of headcount.quartile.share.fte.women[q] * pay.quartile.mean.fte.total[q] / sum of pay.quartile.mean.fte.total[q]. Grade with method.pay-basis, method.headcount-basis and method.scope.

measures.name: Employment parity
measures.definition: Women's share of staff (parity 50%). Other or unreported gender is left out of the denominator.
measures.formula: E = headcount.P.count.women / (headcount.P.count.women + headcount.P.count.men), or headcount.P.share.women where only the share is given. Nivel's base by market: India P = permanent (headcount.permanent.share.women); Japan P = regular (headcount.regular.share.women); UK the mean of the four bands of headcount.quartile.share.hourly.women (full-pay relevant employees); Australia headcount.all.share.women (WGEA); EU headcount.all.count.women and headcount.all.count.men (ESRS S1-6). For route 3 of m.s, use headcount.all.average.* with annual means and headcount.all.fte.* with FTE means. headcount.all.count.other is excluded.

measures.name: Wage parity
measures.definition: Women's mean pay as a share of men's (parity 100%). Exact: a mean on annual total pay, all staff. Approximate: hourly or FTE means, or a subset of staff. Not computable: median-only or adjusted gaps. Outside 30% to 130% it is not comparable and left out of rankings.
measures.formula: W = 1 - pay.all.gap.annual.mean (exact; Japan publishes the ratio itself), 1 - pay.all.gap.hourly.mean (approximate; UK, EU), 1 - pay.all.gap.fte.mean (approximate; Australia), or pay.all.mean.X.women / pay.all.mean.X.men for X = annual, hourly or fte. Subsets, approximate: 1 - pay.regular.gap.annual.mean, 1 - pay.nonregular.gap.annual.mean. India, derived and approximate: W = (S / (1 - S)) * ((1 - E) / E) with S = pay.all.share.annual.women and E = headcount.permanent.share.women. Not W: pay.all.gap.annual.median, pay.all.gap.hourly.median, pay.all.gap.fte.median, pay.all.gap-adjusted.fte, pay.all.gap-adjusted.total; an India estimate from pay.all.median.annual.* and headcount is badged estimated. Check method.pay-basis.

measures.name: Payroll weight
measures.definition: The pay bill that weights each company in an index; an investor owns payroll pro rata to market value (PCAF-style), and each company's weight is its median reported payroll across years. Market value and free float sit outside this catalogue.
measures.formula: payroll = pay.all.total.annual.total. Fallbacks, approximate: headcount.all.count.total * pay.all.mean.annual.total (Japan yuho, filer only) or headcount.all.count.total * pay.all.mean.fte.total (Australia, FTE). headcount.all.size-band.total is not a weight.

measures.name: Gap to parity and its split
measures.definition: How far women's pay falls short of half the payroll, split into too few women employed and women paid less on average.
measures.formula: gap = 0.5 * P - S * P, with P = pay.all.total.annual.total and S from m.s (India: pay.all.share.annual.women). Representation part = P * (0.5 - E); pay part = P * (E - S), E from m.e (India: headcount.permanent.share.women; elsewhere headcount.all.share.women). Each part's share is its sum over index members divided by the sum of both parts.

measures.name: Women on the board
measures.definition: Women's share of board seats, all directors. Japan discloses officers (directors, statutory auditors and executive officers), an approximate route.
measures.formula: seats.board.count.women / seats.board.count.total, or seats.board.share.women; ratio form seats.board.ratio.women-to-men = seats.board.count.women / seats.board.count.men. Japan, approximate: seats.officers.share.women or seats.officers.count.women / (seats.officers.count.women + seats.officers.count.men). seats.board.count.other stays in the total.

measures.name: Board roles held by women
measures.definition: Women in non-executive and executive seats (WoB: 40% of non-executive or 33% of all seats), independent seats, the chair, the four UK senior roles, committees and the CEO.
measures.formula: Non-executive share = seats.board-nonexec.count.women / (seats.board-nonexec.count.women + seats.board-nonexec.count.men), or seats.board-nonexec.share.women; executive share likewise from seats.board-exec.count.*; counts as given: seats.board-independent.count.women, seats.board-chair.count.women, seats.board-senior-roles.count.women (0 to 4), seats.board-committee-chairs.count.women, headcount.ceo.count.women; seats.board-committees.share.women as given.

measures.name: Women in executive management
measures.definition: Women's share of the executive committee; the two levels below the board, KMP or officers are separate, approximate routes.
measures.formula: headcount.executives.count.women / (headcount.executives.count.women + headcount.executives.count.men), or headcount.executives.share.women. Approximate: headcount.topmgmt.share.women (ESRS top management, UK leadership), headcount.kmp.share.women (India), seats.officers.share.women (Japan). headcount.ceo.count.women as given.

measures.name: Women in management by level
measures.definition: Women's share at each management level. Japan's mandatory figure is women's share of managers at section manager level and above.
measures.formula: For L in senior-managers, managers, nonmanagers: headcount.L.count.women / (headcount.L.count.women + headcount.L.count.men), or headcount.L.share.women; supervisors from headcount.supervisors.share.women. Manager category (WGEA) and job category (EEO-1) are qualifiers.

measures.name: Leadership pipeline
measures.definition: How women's share falls with seniority (Equileap criterion 5 compares senior management with the workforce).
measures.formula: Drop at level L = share at L minus headcount.all.share.women, for headcount.supervisors.share.women, headcount.managers.share.women, headcount.senior-managers.share.women, headcount.topmgmt.share.women, headcount.executives.share.women and seats.board.share.women. Pay ladder: upper band of headcount.quartile.share.hourly.women (or headcount.quartile.share.fte.women) minus headcount.all.share.women.

measures.name: Women by pay quartile
measures.definition: Women's share of each pay quartile band and how far the top falls short of the bottom; Nivel's topQuartile is the upper band.
measures.formula: Upper share = headcount.quartile.share.X.women[upper] for X = hourly (UK, PTD), fte (Australia) or annual (PTD); spread = [upper] - [lower]; men's bands from headcount.quartile.share.X.men; band pay levels pay.quartile.mean.fte.total (Australia).

measures.name: Median pay gap
measures.definition: The gap between men's and women's median pay; Australia's headline. Context only: it does not give W.
measures.formula: pay.all.gap.X.median, or 1 - pay.all.median.X.women / pay.all.median.X.men, for X = hourly (UK, PTD), annual (PTD, Spain), fte (Australia); base variants pay.all.gap.fte-base.median and pay.all.gap.hourly-base.median (GRI 105-5).

measures.name: Base pay gap
measures.definition: The gap in base (basic) pay, without variable pay.
measures.formula: pay.all.gap.annual-base.mean = 1 - pay.all.mean.annual-base.women / pay.all.mean.annual-base.men; Australia pay.all.gap.fte-base.mean = 1 - pay.all.mean.fte-base.women / pay.all.mean.fte-base.men, and pay.all.gap.fte-base.median from pay.all.median.fte-base.*; GRI 105-5 pay.all.gap.hourly-base.mean or pay.all.gap.hourly-base.median per category and significant location.

measures.name: Bonus gap and bonus receipt
measures.definition: Bonus and variable pay: the gap among recipients, the gap per worker and who receives it.
measures.formula: pay.recipients.gap.bonus.mean = 1 - pay.recipients.mean.bonus.women / pay.recipients.mean.bonus.men; pay.recipients.gap.bonus.median likewise from pay.recipients.median.bonus.*. Per worker, exact: pay.all.gap.bonus.mean = 1 - (1 - pay.recipients.gap.bonus.mean) * pay.all.rate.bonus.women / pay.all.rate.bonus.men; pay.all.gap.bonus.median only as disclosed. Receipt ratio = pay.all.rate.bonus.women / pay.all.rate.bonus.men; benefits in kind pay.all.rate.benefits-in-kind.women / pay.all.rate.benefits-in-kind.men.

measures.name: Gaps within categories and adjusted gaps
measures.definition: Unequal pay for equal or equal-value work. Shows like-for-like gaps; does not give W.
measures.formula: pay.all.gap.annual-base.mean, pay.all.gap.bonus.mean and pay.all.gap.hourly-base.mean with the category qualifier (PTD Art. 9(1)(g); GRI 105-5); any category gap of 5% or more, unexplained, gives policy.joint-pay-assessment.flag; Spain's 25% rule gives policy.pay-justification.flag; France pay.all.gap-adjusted.fte inside score.fr-index; company models pay.all.gap-adjusted.total.

measures.name: Contract type: pay gaps and concentration
measures.definition: Pay gaps by contract type, and whether women are concentrated in less secure or shorter-hours contracts.
measures.formula: Gaps: pay.regular.gap.annual.mean and pay.nonregular.gap.annual.mean (Japan); pay.parttime.gap.hourly.* and pay.temporary.gap.hourly.* (Ireland). Concentration: women's share of type T = headcount.T.count.women / (headcount.T.count.women + headcount.T.count.men) for T = temporary, nonpermanent, nonguaranteed, parttime, casual, nonregular (or headcount.nonregular.share.women), against the fulltime share and headcount.regular.share.women.

measures.name: Pay at the top
measures.definition: Pay of directors, key executives and managers by gender, with the top-ten count and context ratios.
measures.formula: 1 - pay.board.median.remuneration.women / pay.board.median.remuneration.men and the KMP equivalent (India, median); 1 - pay.board.mean.remuneration.women / pay.board.mean.remuneration.men and the executives equivalent (Spain, mean); women's share of disclosed executive pay = pay.kmp.total.remuneration.women / (pay.kmp.total.remuneration.women + pay.kmp.total.remuneration.men); headcount.top10-earners.count.women out of 10; pay.managers.gap.fte.* and pay.nonmanagers.gap.fte.* as given; context pay.all.ratio.highest-to-median and pay.ceo.ratio.ceo-to-median.

measures.name: Hires
measures.definition: Women's share of hiring against their share of staff.
measures.formula: Share = flows.all.share.hires.women, or flows.all.count.hires.women / (flows.all.count.hires.women + flows.all.count.hires.men); hiring gap = share - headcount.all.share.women; rate ratio = flows.all.rate.hires.women / flows.all.rate.hires.men; Japan flows.all.count.midcareer-hires.*, flows.all.count.rehires.*, flows.all.ratio.applicants-per-hire.*; Italy starting pay pay.new-hires.gap.annual.mean.

measures.name: Leavers and turnover
measures.definition: Whether women leave faster than men.
measures.formula: Turnover ratio = flows.all.rate.leavers.women / flows.all.rate.leavers.men (rate = flows.all.count.leavers.X over headcount); India permanent staff flows.permanent.rate.leavers.women / flows.permanent.rate.leavers.men; Australia voluntary exits flows.all.rate.resignations.* (counts flows.all.count.resignations.*); Spain flows.all.count.dismissals.*; ESRS only flows.all.count.leavers.total and flows.all.rate.leavers.total.

measures.name: Promotions and raises
measures.definition: Whether women are promoted and given raises at men's rate.
measures.formula: Rate ratio = flows.all.rate.promotions.women / flows.all.rate.promotions.men; flows.all.share.promotions.women (or from flows.all.count.promotions.*) against headcount.all.share.women; into management: flows.nonmanagers.count.promotions-to-manager.* and flows.managers.count.appointments.*; France raise gap = flows.all.rate.raises.men - flows.all.rate.raises.women (points); Japan conversions flows.all.count.conversions.*.

measures.name: Parental leave
measures.definition: Who is entitled, who takes leave, who comes back and who stays.
measures.formula: Uptake: leave.entitled.rate.taken.* (ESRS), leave.all.count.taken.X / leave.all.count.entitled.X (GRI), Japan leave.new-parents.rate.childcare.* and leave.new-parents.rate.childcare-or-purpose.men; entitlement leave.all.rate.entitled.total. Return = returned over due to return (leave.all.rate.return.*, counts leave.all.count.returned.*); retention = leave.all.count.retained-12m.X / returned in the prior period = leave.all.rate.retention-12m.*; India leave.permanent.rate.return.* and leave.permanent.rate.retention-12m.*; Australia leave.all.count.left-during-leave.*; France leave.maternity-returners.rate.catch-up-raise.women; policy leave.policy.weeks.paid-parental.

measures.name: Harassment and discrimination complaints
measures.definition: How many complaints are made, how fast they are resolved and how many are upheld.
measures.formula: Rate = complaints.all.count.sexual-harassment * 100 / headcount.all.count.women, or complaints.women.rate.sexual-harassment as reported; resolution = complaints.all.count.sexual-harassment-disposed / complaints.all.count.sexual-harassment; backlog complaints.all.count.sexual-harassment-pending and complaints.all.count.sexual-harassment-pending-90d; upheld share = complaints.all.count.sexual-harassment-upheld / complaints.all.count.sexual-harassment; discrimination complaints.all.count.discrimination and complaints.all.count.discrimination-pending (ESRS 2023: complaints.all.count.discrimination-incl-harassment); context complaints.all.text.actions, training.all.count.harassment-workshops, policy.harassment.flag.

measures.name: Training and reviews
measures.definition: Whether women get as much training and review as men.
measures.formula: Hours ratio = training.all.mean.hours.women / training.all.mean.hours.men; coverage ratios training.all.rate.skills.women / training.all.rate.skills.men, likewise training.all.rate.health-safety.* and training.all.rate.reviews.*.

measures.name: Minimum and living wage
measures.definition: Women's exposure to the wage floor.
measures.formula: Share at minimum wage = headcount.at-minimum-wage.count.women / headcount.all.count.women against headcount.at-minimum-wage.count.men / headcount.all.count.men (India, by category); all-staff context headcount.at-minimum-wage.share.total; headcount.at-or-above-living-wage.share.women against .men (GRI 105-4-c); pay.entry-level.ratio.minimum-wage.women against .men (GRI 202-1); California women's share of each band = headcount.pay-band.count.women / (headcount.pay-band.count.women + headcount.pay-band.count.men), with hours.all.total.* for hourly rates.

measures.name: Benefits, unions and disability
measures.definition: Coverage of well-being benefits and union membership by gender, and women's share of staff with disabilities (mainly India).
measures.formula: For each benefit B in health-insurance, accident-insurance, maternity, paternity, day-care: benefits.all.rate.B.women against benefits.all.rate.B.men; union headcount.permanent.rate.union.women against .men; disability share = headcount.disabled.count.women / (headcount.disabled.count.women + headcount.disabled.count.men).

measures.name: Tenure and long-run retention
measures.definition: Whether women stay as long as men (Japan).
measures.formula: tenure.permanent.gap.years = tenure.permanent.mean.years.men - tenure.permanent.mean.years.women (or as published); retention ratio = flows.hire-cohort.rate.retention-10y.women / flows.hire-cohort.rate.retention-10y.men.

measures.name: Targets and outcomes
measures.definition: Stated gender targets with deadlines and baselines, their outcomes, and compliance with legal quotas.
measures.formula: Progress = (latest actual - baseline) / (target - baseline), with the actual from the matching measure: target.board.share.women with m.board, target.officers.share.women with seats.officers.share.women, target.executives.share.women and target.topmgmt.share.women with m.executives, target.managers.share.women and target.nonmanagers.share.women with m.managers, target.all.share.women with m.e, target.promotions-to-manager.share.women with m.promotions, target.quartile.share.women with m.quartiles, target.all.gap-reduction, target.managers.gap-reduction.fte and target.nonmanagers.gap-reduction.fte with the chosen gap, target.parental-leave.rate.men with m.parental-leave; target.other.list and target.outcome.status as reported; target.board.compliance, target.board-senior-roles.compliance and target.executives.compliance as reported and recomputed from counts.

measures.name: Policies and action plans
measures.definition: Gender policies, plans and external practice scores, recorded as flags and text.
measures.formula: Count of present flags among policy.equal-pay.flag, policy.pay-gap-analysis.flag, policy.joint-pay-assessment.flag, policy.pay-justification.flag, policy.equality-plan.flag, policy.flexible-work.flag, policy.carer-support.flag, policy.domestic-violence-support.flag, policy.harassment.flag, policy.consultation.flag, policy.maternity-compliance.flag, policy.pay-range-in-postings.flag, policy.pay-records.flag; text from policy.action-plan.text, policy.board-diversity.text, policy.diversity-inclusion.text, policy.outsourcing-providers.list, policy.narrative.text; scores score.weps-tool and score.fr-index as reported.

measures.name: Assurance
measures.definition: Whether the gender figures were independently checked, by whom and how far.
measures.formula: Level from assurance.metrics.level (none, assessment, limited, reasonable); assurer assurance.metrics.provider; covered data points assurance.metrics.scope (for example BRSR Core Attribute 6: pay.all.share.annual.women and the POSH complaint figures); attestation assurance.statement.signed.

measures.name: Disclosure basis
measures.definition: How each figure was built; used to grade exactness for every other measure.
measures.formula: method.gender-basis (sex or gender identity; categories), method.headcount-basis (headcount or FTE; period end or average), method.pay-basis (mean or median; elements; exclusions), method.scope (entity, national arm or group; locations), method.pay-coverage.share; headcount.all.count.other gives the size of the other or unreported group.

measures.name: Group and national reconciliation
measures.definition: Ties a group's consolidated profile to its national filings (decision 4). A mismatch is flagged with both figures, never smoothed.
measures.formula: Sum over the group's national arms of headcount.all.count.total <= the group's headcount.all.count.total; for each country c, the group's headcount.national.count.total[c] against the national arm's headcount.all.count.total; the same by gender where both give headcount.all.count.women and headcount.all.count.men; national and group figures (for example a UK and a group pay.all.gap.hourly.mean) never enter one index average. Scope from method.scope.

measures.name: National benchmarks
measures.definition: Official national statistics to set company figures against.
measures.formula: pay.economy.gap.hourly.mean = (pay.economy.mean.hourly.men - pay.economy.mean.hourly.women) / pay.economy.mean.hourly.men (SDG 8.5.1); ILO pay.economy.gap.hourly.median, pay.economy.gap.monthly.mean, pay.economy.gap.monthly.median, pay.economy.gap-factor-weighted.hourly.mean; OECD pay.economy.gap.fulltime.median; SDG 5.5.2 headcount.economy-managers.share.women and headcount.economy-senior-middle-managers.share.women.

measures.name: Other comparisons
measures.definition: Non-gender comparisons in the research that reuse the gender atoms' structure (UK draft ethnicity and disability pay gaps; minority-ethnic director target).
measures.formula: As reported: pay.all.gap-ethnicity.hourly.mean, pay.all.gap-disability.hourly.mean, seats.board.count.minority-ethnic.

catalogue.notes:
LCM catalogue for PARITY-130: 324 data points and 33 measures (5 Nivel tier, 28 wider). Every one of the 92 instruments with measures in measures_compact.json is a source on at least one data point, except UK-SRS, which has no gender measure. Skeleton validated in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-priyanshu-Thoth/48454d65-54cd-4a36-8abe-8225a8e31153/scratchpad/catalogue/ (ids unique, every measure reference resolves, every atom used by a measure). Nothing in the repo was edited.

Id grammar: quantity.population.statistic[.element][.gender]. For gaps the last segment is the average (mean or median), as in pay.all.gap.hourly.mean. For non-pay quantities the element slot names the event, leave type, benefit or item (flows.all.count.hires.women). Policy, target, assurance, method and score atoms use quantity.subject.form. Prefixes hours, tenure, benefits, method and score carry quantity 'other'.

Conventions.
(1) Ratio and gap share one atom. Japan's women-per-100-of-men ratio is pay.all.gap.annual.mean with gap = 1 - ratio, exact.
(2) Breakdowns are observation qualifiers, not atoms: employee category (GRI, SASB, EEO-1 job category, BRSR employees vs workers, Japan employment-management category, Spain classification, France CSP, WGEA manager category and occupation), country, significant location, age band, race, quartile band, leave type. This keeps one atom per concept. Populations that regimes report as distinct bases stay separate atoms: all, permanent, temporary, nonpermanent (BRSR, includes contractor-supplied), nonguaranteed, regular, nonregular, fulltime, parttime, casual, and each level.
(3) Scope (legal entity, national arm, group) is an observation attribute. So one atom holds a UK employer's, a UK national arm's and a group's figure. headcount.national.count.total carries the group's own per-country figure for reconciliation.
(4) Each atom has one canonical period. Stocks are at period end or the snapshot date. headcount.*.average is over the year. Pay totals and annual means are pay actually paid in the year. Hourly is per hour over the year, and a snapshot pay period is graded approximate. FTE is annualised over the 12 months to the snapshot. Bonus is over 12 months. Events and complaints are over the year.
(5) Regime eligibility filters are recorded as approximate mappings, not separate atoms: UK full-pay relevant employees, WGEA exclusions, France Index population, Japan item 3 including dispatched workers.
(6) Gender 'other' covers non-binary and not reported, and is left out of share denominators.

Exactness: exact = mean on annual total pay, all staff, or reported totals and shares. Approximate = hourly or FTE, or a subset. Not computable = median-only or adjusted. The grade is stated in m.s and m.w.

Sources prefixed MAP: come from market_maps.json, not the instrument research:
- IE-GPG: Ireland gender pay gap reports.
- BE-SOCIAL-BALANCE: Belgium's social balance sheet.
- UK-CEO-PAY-RATIO, IN-RULE5, US-SK-402, US-SK-401, AU-CA-S300A.
- IN-AR-EXTRAS: India annual-report governance fields.
- JP-CAO-OFFICERS and JP-NEXTGEN-PLANS.
- US-IL-BCA-14.05.
- FINANCIAL-STATEMENTS.
- VOLUNTARY: company ESG data books, group pay gaps, hires and leavers, targets, assurance.
EU-CSRD is cited for assurance only.

Skeptic corrections applied:
- ESRS 2026 uses EFRAG numbering (S1-5 s19, S1-8 s26, S1-14 s38, S1-15 s40, S1-16 s42); the OJ text is unverified.
- ESRS 2026 drops the gender splits for training, reviews and family-leave uptake, and the non-guaranteed-hours gender split.
- GRI 105-5 final wording is basic hourly, mean or median, per category and location.
- GRI 202-1's gender entry-wage ratio is discontinued in GRI 105, which adds 105-4-c (living wage by gender).
- The PTD pay level is annual and the corresponding hourly. Whether non-recipients count in the variable-pay gap is unresolved, hence two atoms; the per-worker mean is exactly derivable.
- Italy limits pay to fixed, continuing elements.
- Japan WAA corrections: item 3 includes dispatched workers; tenure covers indefinite-term workers; childcare uptake counts statutory leave only.
- India: the ISF wage definition is unverified, and contract staff are not assumed to be in Attribute 6. The e-form employee-by-gender field is not mandatory.
- Illinois 8.12 covers directors per person; executive officers are covered by narrative only.
- Nasdaq rules were deleted 21 Jan 2025.
- California board quotas are struck down, with status after Jan 2025 unchecked.
- An EEO-1 rescission is proposed but not final.
- UK GPG counts biological sex since 21 May 2026.
- WGEA excludes non-binary staff from gaps.

Left out as not gender measures: BRSR P5 EI-6 child labour, forced labour and wage complaints, and S1-7 non-employee counts.
