in.how: Route 1: reported as pay.all.share.annual.women (BRSR P5 EI-3(b), mandatory for the top 1,000 from FY2023-24, assured on the BRSR Core glide path). A mean on total cash pay over all staff on the entity's own payroll. Caveats: contractor-supplied workers' wages are often outside it, and the boundary is standalone or consolidated (method.scope). Route 2 (rupee totals) gives the same share where amounts are filed.

E = headcount.permanent.count.women / (women + men), from BRSR A-20(a) permanent employees plus permanent workers at FY end (Nivel's base, because contract wages are mostly outside the wage totals). All-staff E (headcount.all.share.women) is also exact from A-20(a), but includes contractor-supplied workers. No average or FTE headcount is filed; an opening and closing average needs two filings.

Derived: W = (S / (1 - S)) x ((1 - E) / E) with S = pay.all.share.annual.women and E = permanent share. Approximate because wages are paid over the year to a payroll whose coverage of other-than-permanent staff varies, while E is a year-end permanent headcount. Where S is missing, an estimate from P5 EI-3(a) category medians and headcount is badged estimated. W outside 30-130% is not comparable.

pay.all.total.annual.total from the rupee total wages (XBRL TotalWagesPaid or the printed amount) where filed; the format itself asks only for the %, so for the rest Nivel uses an approximate, badged weight from P5 EI-3(a) medians times headcount. Rupee units vary and are normalised.

gap = P x (0.5 - S), with P = total wages and S reported (P5 EI-3(b)); representation part P x (0.5 - E) and pay part P x (E - S), with E the permanent share. Exact where P is filed; approximate where P is the median-based estimate.

seats.board.count.women / seats.board.count.total, or seats.board.share.women, from BRSR A-21 (executive and non-executive directors pooled); the men's count comes from P5 EI-3(a). LODR Reg 17(1)(a) and Companies Act s.149(1) set a floor of one woman.

No statutory item splits directors by role and gender: non-executive, executive, independent, chair and CEO are named in the corporate governance report without a gender field, so Nivel infers them by reading. Only the committee share is computable, from voluntary GRI 405-1-a and 2-9-c-v reports (seats.board-committees.share.women, available).
in.fixed: The how itself says committee shares exist, and seats.board-committees.share.women is an available cell, so part of the measure is computable. 'Not computable' should mean nothing can be computed; the UK and EU grade the same partial situation approximate.

in.how: headcount.kmp.share.women from BRSR A-21: statutory KMP (CEO or MD, whole-time directors, CFO, company secretary), usually 3 to 6 people, so narrower than an executive committee. Voluntary SASB executive-management shares exist for IT services and some financials (group scope).

Only voluntary GRI 405-1-b and SASB category shares, with company-defined levels and group scope. BRSR's split of employees and workers (IR Code s.2(zr)) is not a management split, though workers sit below management.
Board (A-21) and KMP (A-21) shares against headcount.all.share.women are statutory; manager levels only from voluntary GRI 405-1-b categories. No pay quartiles, so no pay ladder.
No pay quartiles are disclosed in India.

1 - women's median / men's median, annual, per P5 EI-3(a) category (employees other than board and KMP; workers; also board and KMP). No all-staff median, and the pay concept (remuneration, salary or wages) is not fixed.
Only voluntary GRI 405-2 ratios of basic salary of women to men, by employee category and significant location, with mean or median and time unit unspecified (group scope).
No bonus data are disclosed; bonuses sit inside gross wages.
Statutory P5 EI-3(a) category median ratios (board, KMP, employees, workers) and voluntary GRI 405-2 category ratios. No joint pay assessment, Spanish 25% rule or France Index applies.

Concentration only: women's share of other-than-permanent staff (headcount.nonpermanent.count.*, A-20(a)) against the permanent share; voluntary GRI 2-7 adds temporary, part-time and full-time. No pay gap by contract type.

1 - board median women / men and the KMP equivalent, from P5 EI-3(a) medians (exact as medians; board medians pool executive pay with non-executive sitting fees). Context pay.ceo.ratio.ceo-to-median from Rules 2014 r.5(1)(i) (exact where the CEO is a director). Board means and the women KMP total are approximate from median times count (exact for one or two people).
Hires by gender only from voluntary GRI 401-1-a or WEPs (group scope); the hiring gap against headcount.all.share.women mixes that scope with BRSR's entity headcount.

flows.permanent.rate.leavers.women / .men from BRSR A-22 (permanent employees and permanent workers, average of opening and closing headcount, three-year trend). All-staff rates only from voluntary GRI 401-1-b.
Only the voluntary WEPs share of promotions (and counts some reports volunteer) against headcount.all.share.women; no promotion rates.

Return and 12-month retention rates by gender for permanent staff from BRSR P3 EI-5 (GRI formulas). Entitlement and uptake only from voluntary GRI 401-3; statutory maternity and paternity benefit coverage from P3 EI-1.

Rate as reported (P5 EI-7, % of female employees and workers) or complaints x 100 / headcount.all.count.women; upheld share from P5 EI-7; resolution from IN-CAR-2025 disposed over received; backlog from P5 EI-6 pending and CAR-2025 pending over 90 days; discrimination from P5 EI-6. POSH Rule 14 items (workshops, actions) are filed on a calendar year and not public.
Coverage ratios from BRSR P3 EI-8 (health and safety; skill upgradation) and P3 EI-9 (reviews), by gender. The hours ratio needs voluntary GRI 404-1.

Share at minimum wage by gender from BRSR P5 EI-2 counts over category totals, for permanent and other-than-permanent employees and workers. Entry-level ratios only from voluntary GRI 202-1; no living-wage or pay-band data.
BRSR P3 EI-1 coverage by gender for health insurance, accident insurance, maternity, paternity and day care; union membership from P3 EI-7; disability share from A-20(b).
No tenure or hire-cohort retention is disclosed in India.

Gender targets appear only where a company sets them under BRSR Section B Q5, with performance in Q6; actuals come from the matching statutory measure (board, KMP, workforce share). Board rule compliance is recomputed from the women count for the one-woman floor only.

Two statutory flags: the Internal Complaints Committee statement and the Maternity Benefit Act compliance statement (IN-CAR-2025). Equal pay is a legal duty (Code on Wages s.3) but not disclosed; the other flags are not asked.
Level and provider from BRSR Section A Q14-15; scope fixed by BRSR Core Attribute 6 (wage share and POSH complaints), on the glide path top 500 in FY2025-26 and top 1,000 from FY2026-27.

Gender and headcount bases are fixed by the format (male and female, optional other; FY-end headcount); scope from Section A Q13. The pay basis rests on ISF standards known only from a summary, and pay coverage is not stated.

Each Indian listed filer gives entity headcount by gender (A-20(a)), and every company's Extract of Board Report e-form has an FY-end headcount field by gender (item (j), unstarred, filed on MCA21), so a group's Indian filers can be summed where they file. Group headcount by country is only in voluntary GRI 2-7 regions, and a consolidated BRSR is itself group scope, so the check is partial.
in.fixed: 'Every company gives FY-end headcount' overstates an unstarred e-form field (IN-CAR-2025 check: item (j) not starred; rule 8(5) has no gender headcount). Grade unchanged.

in.how: SDG 8.5.1 mean hourly earnings by sex and SDG 5.5.2 management shares from MoSPI survey data (UN SDG database, ILOSTAT); ILO Global Wage Report mean, median, monthly and factor-weighted gaps are periodic. The OECD full-time median gap does not cover India.
No ethnicity or disability pay gap and no minority-ethnic board count are asked in India.

uk.how: Route 3 only, per GB legal employer: W = 1 - pay.all.gap.hourly.mean (UK-GPG-2017 Reg 2(1)(a)) and E = mean of the four headcount.quartile.share.hourly.women (Reg 2(1)(f)), both on full-pay relevant employees in the April pay period; a group's UK arm combines its employers by size-band midpoints. Hourly, so women's fewer paid hours are missed and S overstates the annual share. Routes 1 and 2 are not available (no pay totals by sex) and route 4 is not (no quartile pay levels). A group S needs a voluntary worldwide mean gap (Bloomberg Q29f) with s414C E, also approximate.

Group: exact from s.414C(8)(c)(iii) year-end counts by sex, UK-incorporated quoted companies only. UK arm (Nivel's base): the mean of the four hourly quartile shares, exact for each employer's full-pay relevant employees, approximate across a multi-employer group (size-band weights) and for all staff. No average or FTE headcount by sex, so route 3 pairs the quartile E with the hourly W on the same staff.

W = 1 - pay.all.gap.hourly.mean per legal employer: hourly mean, ordinary pay plus pro-rated bonus, full-pay relevant employees; check the 30 to 130% range. No annual or FTE gap and no pay levels by sex. The median gap (Reg 2(1)(b)) is not W. A group W only from voluntary sources (GRI 405-2 ratios, Bloomberg Q29f), approximate.

No UK pay total in the research: none of the 12 UK instruments requires wages or a pay bill, and the GPG service gives a size band, which is not a weight. Nivel weights UK companies equally today. Companies Act 2006 s.411 staff costs could give a group payroll once a verified record is added to the research.
uk.fixed: The approximate grade rested only on UK-CA2006-S411, which the cell itself says is outside the research inputs (see the pay.all.total.annual.total fix). The UK market map confirms payroll fields are always empty for GB.

uk.how: Needs P and S on one scope. No P exists in the research at national or group scope (see m.payroll), so neither the representation part nor the pay part can be computed. Never pair a group P with a national S.
uk.fixed: The group route used P from s.411, which is not supported by the research.

uk.how: seats.board.share.women, or count.women / count.total, from UKLR 6 Annex 1R Table 1 (reference date; sex or gender identity; other and not specified rows kept in the total), FY2022-23 onward, all commercial companies and trusts. s.414C(8)(c)(i) gives directors by sex at year end from 2013 for UK-incorporated quoted companies. The ratio form follows from the counts.

Only seats.board-senior-roles.count.women (UKLR Table 1, 0 to 4) is statutory, with the senior-role compliance statement. No non-executive or executive split by sex, and no independent, chair, CEO or committee-chair counts; the committee share only voluntarily (GRI 2-9-c-v).

headcount.executives.count.* and share.women from UKLR 6 Annex 1R Table 1 (ExCo or most senior body below the board, including the company secretary). The CEO alone is not available. Approximate alternative: headcount.topmgmt.share.women (Code Provision 23 and the Women Leaders Review, ExCo plus direct reports).

Senior managers exact from s.414C(8)(c)(ii) counts (function-based, including subsidiary directors; UK-incorporated quoted companies). Managers and non-managers only voluntarily, as shares in company-defined categories (GRI 405-1-b, SASB). Supervisors not available.

Board and executives (UKLR), top management (Provision 23, comply or explain), senior managers (s414C) and all staff (s414C group counts) give a group ladder; managers only voluntarily, supervisors not. Pay ladder: upper hourly quartile minus the quartile-mean share, exact per UK employer. The group ladder and the UK-employer quartiles are different scopes and stay apart.

Upper share, spread and men's bands from Reg 2(1)(f) hourly quartiles per legal employer, all four bands; a group's UK arm is approximate (size-band weights). No FTE quartiles; annual-style quartiles only voluntarily (Bloomberg Q29b-e); no band pay levels.
pay.all.gap.hourly.median from Reg 2(1)(b) per legal employer. Medians cannot be combined exactly across a group's employers. No annual, FTE or base median gaps.

Voluntary only: GRI 405-2-a basic salary ratio per category and location (time unit and mean or median left open) and WEF's mean basic salary gap of full-time staff. No statutory base pay gap; GRI 105-5 basic hourly gaps are not yet effective.

Recipients' mean and median bonus gaps and the bonus receipt rates from Reg 2(1)(c) to (e); the per-worker mean gap follows exactly from the formula. Per-worker median, bonus levels and benefits in kind are not available.

Only voluntary GRI 405-2 ratios per employee category and significant location (basic salary and remuneration); adjusted gaps only where companies publish them (Bloomberg Q28). No joint pay assessment, Spain or France equivalents.

No pay gaps by contract type in the UK. Concentration only from voluntary GRI 2-7-b counts (temporary, non-guaranteed hours, full-time and part-time by gender). Non-permanent staff are approximated by GRI temporary employees, which leaves out contractor-supplied workers. No casual or regular categories.
uk.fixed: Follows the headcount.nonpermanent fixes, which align the UK with the AU derivation.

uk.how: No pay by sex for directors or executives. The CEO pay ratio (SI 2018/860, UK employees, proposed for removal) and the voluntary highest-to-median ratio (WEF) are context only.
Voluntary only: GRI 401-1-a counts and rates by gender and the WEPs share of hires; hiring gap against the s414C group share. No Japan or Italy variants.
Voluntary only: GRI 401-1-b turnover counts and rates by gender and in total. No resignation, dismissal or permanent-staff variants.
Only women's share of promotions, voluntarily (WEPs indicator 6, Bloomberg Q14), against the s414C share. No counts or rates by sex, no promotions into management, raises or conversions.

Voluntary only: GRI 401-3 entitled, taken, returned and retained counts and rates by gender; uptake = taken / entitled; the entitlement share is approximate against s414C headcount. No disclosure of paid-leave weeks.

No UK rule on sexual harassment complaints (the Worker Protection Act 2023 has no reporting). Only voluntary discrimination incident counts and actions (GRI 406-1, all grounds, not by gender) and a voluntary harassment policy flag.
Voluntary only: GRI 404-1 average training hours and 404-3 review coverage by gender. Skills and health and safety coverage (India) are not available.

Only GRI 202-1 entry-level wage ratios to the minimum wage by gender (voluntary, significant locations, dropped in GRI 105). No minimum-wage or living-wage shares by sex; GRI 105-4 is not yet effective.
No UK disclosure of benefit coverage, union membership or disability by sex.
No UK disclosure of tenure or long-run retention by sex.

Board: UKLR compliance statements against the rule's 40% and senior-role thresholds, recomputable from Table 1 counts. Company-set board targets are voluntary, in own reports only. Top management: the Review's voluntary 40% leadership target against Provision 23 or Review actuals. No executive, manager, workforce, pay gap or leave targets; action plans set actions, not numbers.
uk.fixed: The UKLR 40% is a compliance threshold, not a company target (see the target.board.share.women fix).

uk.how: Flags: pay gap analysis (every GPG filing), equality action plan (voluntary from April 2026, expected mandatory in 2027), harassment policy (Bloomberg, voluntary). No equal pay policy flag: the Scottish equal pay statement binds Scottish public authorities only. Texts: action plan, board diversity policy (DTR 7.2.8AR, mandatory), D&I policy (Provision 23), GPG narrative. Outsourcing providers enacted but not in force. A flag count rests on a partial set.
uk.fixed: The equal pay statement is removed, as UK-SCOT-PSED-2012 does not cover companies (see the policy.equal-pay.flag fix).

uk.how: Only the GPG signed statement of accuracy is statutory. Level, provider and scope only where companies report voluntary assurance (GRI 2-5); GPG and UKLR figures are not audited.

Gender basis from UKLR 6.6.6R(11) (sex or gender identity); GPG and s414C use sex by rule. Headcount, pay and scope bases are fixed by each instrument (GPG snapshot headcount, hourly pay rules, legal entity; s414C year end, consolidation), with GRI 2-7-c voluntary. Pay coverage share voluntary only (Bloomberg Q29a). Other or unstated rows from UKLR for boards.

Group headcount by sex from s414C (UK-incorporated quoted companies only). The UK arm has no real headcount, only each employer's size band, so the sum check uses band midpoints. Group headcount by country only voluntarily (GRI 2-7 regions). UK-employer hourly gaps and any group gap stay in separate averages.

SDG 8.5.1 mean hourly earnings and gap, SDG 5.5.2 management shares and the OECD full-time median gap are published for the UK; the ILO monthly, median and factor-weighted gaps are one-off Global Wage Report estimates (approximate). ONS ASHE gives the official UK median gap.
Board minority-ethnic count statutory (UKLR Table 2). Ethnicity pay gap voluntary only (WEF, company reports) and proposed mandatory; disability pay gap proposed only.

au.how: Route 3: E = headcount.all.share.women (WGEA total workforce % women) and W = 1 - pay.all.gap.fte.mean (WGEA mean annualised FTE total remuneration gap), giving women's share of FTE pay for each corporate group's Australian staff. Approximate: FTE annualisation grosses up part-time and casual pay, more often women's, so it overstates women's share of pay actually paid. Route 4 (quartile shares times quartile average pay) is an approximate cross-check. Not computable for 2022-23, which has medians only. National scope; a worldwide group figure only from company reports.

headcount.all.share.women from WGEA (women over women and men, headcount on the snapshot date, all Australian employees), or from GEI 1 counts back to 2014-15. A snapshot, not a period average; excludes non-binary staff, contractors and agency workers.
W = 1 - pay.all.gap.fte.mean on annualised FTE total remuneration, from 2023-24. Median gaps (from 2022-23) are not W. Flag W outside 30-130% as not comparable.

headcount.all.count.total (exact, WGEA) times pay.all.mean.fte.total (WGEA average total remuneration, FTE, rounded to the nearest thousand dollars). No pay bill is published; the FTE product overstates pay actually paid for part-time, casual and part-year staff.
P from m.payroll and S from m.s, both FTE-based; E = headcount.all.share.women is exact. The representation part P(0.5 - E) is as good as P; the pay part P(E - S) carries the FTE approximation.

seats.board.share.women for the listed board from ASX Rec 1.5 (comply or explain, group), or counts from WGEA Q1.5d (mandatory, per reporting ABN's governing body, which may be a subsidiary board). Ratio from the counts. Japan officers not applicable.

Chair gender exact from WGEA Q1.5d and CEO gender exact from WGEA. Executive and non-executive seats only from directors named in the annual report, with gender read from names. Committee composition by gender only voluntarily (GRI 2-9-c-v). The research has no independent-director or committee-chair counts by gender: ASX Recs 2.1 to 8.1 are not in it. Australian boards rarely have a senior independent director.
au.fixed: Follows the fixes to seats.board-independent, seats.board-committees and seats.board-committee-chairs.

au.how: ASX Rec 1.5 senior executive proportions use each entity's own definition, usually group-wide. WGEA CEO plus KMP counts (Australian staff per ABN) stand in for the executive committee; WGEA top-level management (CEO, heads of business, KMP, other executives) approximates ESRS top management.
WGEA counts by gender for senior managers, all managers and non-managers per ABN (GEI 1), summable to the national arm. Japan supervisors not applicable.

Drops at all managers, senior managers and the board are exact from WGEA and ASX; top management and executives are approximate (WGEA categories); no supervisor level. Pay ladder: upper FTE quartile share (exact) minus headcount.all.share.women.

headcount.quartile.share.fte.women and .men and pay.quartile.mean.fte.total are published by WGEA, ranked on annualised FTE total remuneration. Annual-style quartiles only voluntarily (Bloomberg Q29b-e, group); no hourly ranking.
au.fixed: The current how says annual rankings do not exist, which the Bloomberg Q29b-e fix contradicts.

au.how: pay.all.gap.fte.median and pay.all.gap.fte-base.median published from 2022-23 (2022-23 excludes CEO pay, so it is not comparable with later years). No hourly or annual medians; median pay levels are not published.
pay.all.gap.fte-base.mean (from 2023-24) and pay.all.gap.fte-base.median (from 2022-23) published by WGEA. Base pay levels are not published; GRI 405-2-a category ratios are voluntary.
WGEA has no bonus or bonus-receipt measures. The total minus base gap mixes bonuses with superannuation, overtime and allowances, so it is not a bonus gap.

No statutory category or adjusted gaps; WGEA Q2.2a records only whether a like-for-like analysis was done. Inputs are voluntary GRI 405-2-a ratios by category and location, and Bloomberg Q28 adjusted gaps where companies publish them (group). The s 13 manager and non-manager gaps are not public until WGEA publishes target baselines. No joint pay assessment, Spain rule or France Index.
au.fixed: Follows the pay.all.gap-adjusted.total and pay.managers or nonmanagers gap fixes.

au.how: Concentration exact from WGEA counts of permanent, fixed-term (contract), casual, full-time and part-time staff by gender. Non-permanent is approximate (contractor-supplied workers excluded); non-guaranteed hours via casuals or voluntary GRI 2-7. Pay gaps by contract type are not published.

The s 300A remuneration report gives each director's and KMP's pay by name, so board and KMP medians and means and women's share of disclosed executive pay are computable, with gender read from names. Manager and non-manager FTE gaps are not public: WGEA's Executive Summary is confidential and s 13 target baselines are not yet published. Highest-to-median only voluntarily (WEF, GRI 2-21), per country. No CEO pay ratio and no top-ten earners.
au.fixed: Follows the pay.managers or nonmanagers gap fixes and the pay.all.ratio.highest-to-median exactness fix.

au.how: WGEA external appointments by gender give hire counts, share and rates over snapshot headcount, and the hiring gap against headcount.all.share.women. Japan hiring items and Italy's starting pay gap not applicable.

Nationally WGEA counts resignations (voluntary exits) only, so the turnover ratio uses flows.all.rate.resignations, the Australian variant. All-exit turnover by gender only from voluntary GRI 401-1-b (group). Permanent-staff rate from permanent resignations. No dismissals.

WGEA promotions by gender (counts, share and rate over headcount), promotions from non-manager to manager, and internal and external appointments into management. France raises and Japan conversions not applicable.

WGEA gives primary and secondary carer's leave taken by gender, employees who left during paid parental leave, and weeks of employer-funded leave. Uptake among the entitled, return and 12-month retention only from voluntary GRI 401-3 (group).

No instrument requires sexual harassment complaint counts; WGEA Q5.7 asks only whether such data is collected. Discrimination incidents and actions only from voluntary GRI 406-1 (group). Context: policy.harassment.flag (WGEA GEI 6).
Voluntary only: GRI 404-1 average training hours and 404-3 review coverage by gender (group). Health and safety and skills training by gender (India) are not available; nothing statutory.
au.fixed: The same facts are graded exact for the UK, which uses the same voluntary GRI 404 sources and the same missing India items. Exactness grades the basis, not whether a disclosure is mandatory.

au.how: Only voluntary GRI 202-1 entry-level wage to minimum wage by gender (group). No minimum-wage or living-wage counts by gender, no pay bands.
No benefit coverage, union membership or disability counts by gender; WGEA asks policy questions only.
Length of service and hire-cohort retention are not collected.

WGEA DRE targets (ss 7-13, 17) use baselines equal to WGEA published values, so progress will be exact once WGEA publishes the selections (not yet at 12 Oct 2026); outcomes under s 17C from the 2028-29 report. Board target % and year from WGEA Q1.5g; ASX Rec 1.5 objectives are entity-defined. Board objective compliance computable against 30% for the S&P/ASX 300.

8 of the 13 flags exist and are mandatory WGEA answers per ABN: equal pay, gap analysis (with date), gender equality policy, flexible work, carer support, family and domestic violence, harassment, consultation. Joint pay assessment, pay justification, maternity compliance, pay range and pay records have no Australian counterpart and count as absent. Text from the ASX Rec 1.5 diversity policy and WGEA Employer Statements; the WEPs Tool score is confidential.
No mandatory assurance of WGEA or ASX figures; WGEA reports carry a CEO sign-off. Level, provider and scope only from voluntary GRI 2-5.

Gender, headcount and pay bases and the reporting scope are fixed nationally by WGEA, so they are exact. The covered share of staff is given only voluntarily (Bloomberg Q29a, group), and other-gender counts only voluntarily (GRI 2-7); WGEA does not publish non-binary counts.
au.fixed: Bloomberg Q29a supplies the covered share voluntarily (see the method.pay-coverage.share fix). That leaves AU in the same position as the UK, whose m.basis is graded exact.

au.how: National totals exact from WGEA (group info sheet, and ABN counts by gender from the public dataset). Group worldwide headcount and any Australian line only from voluntary GRI 2-7. WGEA's snapshot date (within 1 Apr to 31 Mar) differs from 30 June financial years and excludes contractors, so allow a tolerance and flag mismatches.

As reported: SDG 8.5.1 hourly earnings and gap, SDG 5.5.2 management shares and the OECD median full-time gap cover Australia; ILO variants where covered. Not comparable with WGEA employer gaps or the ABS full-time ordinary-time gap.
Ethnicity pay gap only voluntarily (WEF-SCM pay gap by diversity indicators, group). No disability pay gap or minority ethnic director count in Australia.
au.fixed: Follows the pay.all.gap-ethnicity.hourly.mean fix. The UK grades the same WEF source approximate.

jp.how: No total-pay or share disclosure, so routes 1, 2 and 4 are out. Route 3: W = 1 - pay.all.gap.annual.mean, the WAA mean on annual total pay over all workers (the exact pay input), with E from the optional WAA workforce item. E is the weak side: it is not the average monthly headcount the ratio uses, the all-workers row is rare and can include dispatched workers, and Nivel today pairs all-worker W with regular-staff E (headcount.regular.share.women), which mixes bases. Like-for-like option: pay.regular.gap.annual.mean with headcount.regular.share.women gives the regular-staff share of regular pay, approximate as a subset. E is missing for about 30% of companies.

headcount.regular.share.women (Nivel's Japan base) comes from the optional WAA workforce item (Art 19(1)(iii)ハ), regular-staff row: a subset of staff. An all-workers row is rare and can include dispatched workers. Counts by gender exist only in voluntary GRI 2-7 data, usually group-wide. No average or FTE headcount by gender, so the E that would make route 3 exact is never published.

Japan publishes W itself: women's mean annual total pay (salary, allowances, bonuses) as a % of men's, all workers of the legal entity, total wages over average monthly headcount (WAA Art 19(1)(i), repeated in the securities report). W = value / 100. It turns approximate where an employer converts part-timers to FTE or excludes allowances (stated, see method.headcount-basis and method.pay-basis). Mandatory regular and non-regular ratios give subset W, approximate. Apply the 30-130% rule; the pipeline's 20-150% filter is wider.

No payroll total. Fallback: headcount.all.count.total times pay.all.mean.annual.total from the securities report, filer only. Both exclude temporary staff (shown separately as an annual average), so the weight understates the payroll the WAA ratio covers. Not by gender. The MHLW size band is not a weight.

P from the payroll fallback (filer only), S from route 3 (approximate), E from headcount.regular.share.women or headcount.all.share.women (optional). The representation part P*(0.5 - E) and pay part P*(E - S) follow, all approximate, and only for companies with an E.

The statutory figure is officers, not the board: the securities report gives men and women officers and the women's share (directors, statutory auditors and 執行役) as of the filing date, so seats.officers.share.women stands in. It equals the board share at companies with an audit and supervisory committee (no statutory auditors, no 執行役). Directors-only counts and shares only in voluntary GRI 2-9 and 405-1-a data. Board size is countable from the officer list. MHLW item 11 (company-defined officers, median 20.5 people) is not a board count.

No instrument gives the gender of the chair, CEO, executive, non-executive or independent directors, or committee chairs. Only women's share of committee seats is computable, from voluntary GRI 405-1-a data (seats.board-committees.share.women, available).
jp.fixed: seats.board-committees.share.women is an available Japan cell (GRI-405-2016 405-1-a), so the measure is partly computable; the UK and EU grade partial coverage approximate.

jp.how: No executive count by gender is required. Stand-ins: seats.officers.share.women (includes 執行役 only at companies with nominating committees; 執行役員 excluded) or voluntary headcount.executives.share.women (SASB executive management, four industries). TSE Rule 445-7 lets companies count 執行役員 as officers, so its figures differ from the securities report.

headcount.managers.share.women is statutory and defined (section-manager level and above, officers excluded): WAA Art 19(1)(ii), mandatory for 101+ employers from the first business year ending on or after 1 April 2026, and in the securities report since FY ending March 2023 where published; counts are in the MHLW database for about half of listed employers. Supervisors (係長級) from an optional WAA item. Senior managers only as a voluntary WEPs share. Non-managers only approximately, by subtracting managers from a derived workforce count.

Levels available: supervisors (optional WAA), managers (statutory), officers as the board stand-in (statutory); executives and senior managers only voluntarily; no top-management level and no pay quartiles. The baseline headcount.all.share.women is optional and mostly given for regular staff only, so drops are measured against regular staff for most companies.
No quartile or pay-band disclosure in Japan. The MHLW database's optional extra pay-ratio categories (grade, course, job type) are not quartiles.
The WAA ratio and the securities report are means only; no instrument asks for a median.
No statutory base-pay gap: the WAA ratio includes allowances and bonuses. Only voluntary GRI 405-2-a ratios of basic salary by employee category and significant location, mean or median unstated.
Bonuses sit inside the WAA total-pay ratio and are never split out; no bonus receipt rates.

WAA requires the ratio by employment-management category (at least regular and non-regular) and lets employers add up to five more categories (grade, course, job type; 45 listed employers do) with notes, on annual total pay, not base pay. Company-defined like-for-like comparisons appear in notes (pay.all.gap-adjusted.total). Voluntary GRI 405-2 by category. No joint pay assessment, Spanish 25% rule or France index.

The measure's Japan gaps are statutory: pay.regular.gap.annual.mean and pay.nonregular.gap.annual.mean, means on annual total pay. Concentration: headcount.regular.share.women against the non-regular rows of the optional WAA workforce item (usually separate contract, part-time and dispatched rows, so that half is approximate); temporary, full-time and part-time counts by gender only in voluntary GRI 2-7. No hourly part-time or temporary gaps.

Officer pay is disclosed by officer category and for individuals paid 100 million yen or more, never by gender; no board, KMP or executive pay by gender. Context only: CEO-to-median and highest-to-median ratios in voluntary WEF metrics.

Women's share of hires is an optional WAA item, published by employment-management category, so the all-hires share is exact only from voluntary GRI 401-1-a counts (approximate from the category rows). Mid-career hires, rehires and applicants per hire by sex are optional WAA items. Hiring gap uses headcount.all.share.women (optional). No starting-pay gap.

No statutory turnover by gender; the turnover ratio is exact only from voluntary GRI 401-1-b rates. Statutory proxies are optional WAA items: average tenure by gender and retention about 10 years after hire (m.tenure). No resignation, dismissal or permanent-staff rates.

No statutory promotion counts. Women's share of promotions only from voluntary WEPs reporting; conversions to regular contracts by sex from an optional WAA item. No promotion rates, appointments to management or raises.

Men's uptake is statutory (CCLA Ordinance Art 71-6, option (i) childcare leave or option (ii) including childcare-purpose leave, the option stated; more than 300 workers from April 2025; in the securities report). Women's uptake by category is an optional WAA item. Both divide by births in the year (can exceed 100%), not by entitled staff, so they are not ESRS uptake. Entitlement, return and 12-month retention only in voluntary GRI 401-3, from which ESRS-style uptake is exact.

No disclosure duty for harassment complaints in Japan; prevention measures are required but not reported. Only the discrimination part is computable, from voluntary GRI 406-1 incidents (all grounds, not by gender) with status and actions.
jp.fixed: complaints.all.count.discrimination, discrimination-pending, discrimination-incl-harassment and complaints.all.text.actions are available Japan cells (GRI-406-2016), and the measure includes them (India's m.harassment uses P5 EI-6 discrimination too), so it is partly computable, not 'not computable'.

jp.how: Hours and review-coverage ratios are exact only from voluntary GRI 404-1 and 404-3 data; no health-and-safety or skills training by gender.
Only voluntary GRI 202-1 entry-level wage ratios to the local (prefectural) minimum wage by gender at significant locations. No counts at minimum wage, living-wage shares or pay bands.
India BRSR items; nothing comparable is disclosed in Japan, and disability employment reporting is not public or by gender.

Both parts are optional WAA items with MHLW database fields: men's and women's average years of service for indefinite-term workers (the item is the difference) and the share of each sex still employed about 10 years after hire. The securities report's average tenure is not by gender.

Targets exist but each company picks them: WAA action plans must carry numeric targets (101+ employers; 301+ at least two); the securities report must give human-capital metrics, targets and results; the Corporate Governance Code asks for measurable diversity targets for core staff (comply or explain); the Next-Generation Act requires a men's childcare-leave target (more than 100 workers, from April 2025); TSE Prime companies are asked to aim for 30% women officers by 2030. Progress is computable only where a target matches a disclosed measure (managers, officers, men's leave, hires, pay ratio).

Statutory: the equality (action) plan flag and text (WAA Art 8), the diversity policy (securities-report human-capital strategy) and the pay gap analysis flag, computable from each published WAA ratio. Comply or explain: board diversity (Code Principle 4-13(1)). Optional: pay-ratio notes and MHLW database programme flags (flex-time, telework, short hours). No equal-pay, harassment, carer, consultation or pay-range flags; no WEPs Tool or France scores.
jp.fixed: Follows the policy.pay-gap-analysis.flag fix (computable from pay.all.gap.annual.mean, JP-WAA Ordinance Art 19(1)(i)); grade unchanged.

jp.how: No assurance duty for these figures: the securities report's non-financial sections are not audited and MHLW data is self-reported. The representative's confirmation letter (確認書) covers the whole securities report. Voluntary third-party assurance appears in some ESG data books (GRI 2-5: level, provider, scope). SSBJ assurance, from FY ending March 2028 for the largest companies, covers emissions and governance first.

Headcount basis (default headcount, optional FTE conversion of part-timers, stated) and pay basis (excluded allowances stated; period) come with the WAA ratio; scope from the securities report's per-entity table and the MHLW data-scope field (86 listed rows are group-wide, which the pipeline does not yet read). The gender basis is fixed as men and women by the forms, never stated as sex or gender identity, and pay coverage is not given.
jp.fixed: Follows the method.gender-basis fix (JP-FSA-ORD form '男性 名 女性 名'); the 86 group-wide rows were confirmed in MHLW CSV column 220 ('グループ（連結等）' for 86 listed rows). Grade unchanged.

jp.how: The securities report gives the filer's and the consolidated group's employee totals, so filer <= group can be checked exactly, and lists the WAA figures for each domestic consolidated subsidiary that publishes them (the nearest thing to a national arm, but without headcount by gender to weight them). No group headcount by gender or by country (only voluntary GRI 2-7 by region). Holding companies are often exempt and their operating subsidiaries carry the figures. Entity figures and any group-wide figure from the annual report stay apart.

Japan's economy-wide series exist outside company filings: ILO SDG 8.5.1 hourly earnings and gap, ILO mean and median hourly and monthly variants and the factor-weighted gap (periodic), the OECD median full-time gap, and SDG 5.5.2 women in total and in senior and middle management. Context only.
No ethnicity or disability pay gap or minority-ethnic board count is asked for in Japan.

eu.how: Route 3 at group level, as Nivel does today: S = E*W/(E*W+1-E) with W = 1 - pay.all.gap.hourly.mean (ESRS S1-16 §97(a), mean hourly, total pay) and E = headcount.all.count.women / (women + men) (ESRS S1-6 §50(a)). Approximate: an hourly W with a headcount E, company-chosen pay elements and scope; 73 of 103 Nivel companies have both. Route 1 does not exist, as no EU rule asks for S. Route 2 comes only from Italy's art. 46 total pay by sex per entity, which covers a biennium and is not public, so it is approximate too; Belgium's personnel costs by gender (NBB, market map) give an approximate public entity route. From 2027 (2026 pay year), per employer: W = 1 - pay.all.gap.annual.mean and E = the mean of headcount.quartile.share.annual.women (PTD Art. 9(1)(a) and (f)), approximate in Italy, whose pay level leaves out non-structural pay. Spain: W from EINF mean annual pay by sex (company-defined pay). Not computable where S1-16 is declared not material (8 of 103) or only adjusted or partial gaps are given (13). W outside 30-130% is not comparable.
eu.fixed: The how called Route 2 'exact' from Italy's art. 46 totals, but IT-ART46's period is the 'biennium' and the crosswalk grades those totals approximate.

eu.how: E = headcount.all.count.women / (headcount.all.count.women + headcount.all.count.men) from ESRS S1-6 §50(a), group, with headcount.all.count.other left out; method.headcount-basis (§50(d)) says year end or average. India's permanent-staff base comes from §50(b) permanent counts (head count or FTE as disclosed). Entity level: Germany's § 21 average headcount by sex every 3 or 5 years; from 2027 the mean of each employer's PTD quartile shares.

W = 1 - pay.all.gap.hourly.mean (ESRS S1-16 §97(a)): an hourly mean, group-wide, on company-chosen pay elements. An annual W = 1 - pay.all.gap.annual.mean comes per employer from the PTD (Art. 9(1)(a), total pay, all workers) from 2027, approximate as transposed in Italy (fixed elements only). Spain's EINF means by sex give a group annual W on company-defined pay. Not W: France's Index gap (adjusted), ESRS AR 33 adjusted gaps and the PTD median gaps.

No gender regime discloses the pay bill. pay.all.total.annual.total comes from the IFRS consolidated employee benefits expense, which includes employer social and pension costs (outside the verified research). Entity totals: Italy's art. 46 women plus men (not public) and Belgium's personnel costs (NBB, market map). The ESRS remuneration ratio is not a weight.

P from IFRS personnel expense (approximate); S from m.s (approximate); E = headcount.all.share.women (exact, ESRS S1-6). The representation part P*(0.5 - E) is as good as P; the pay part P*(E - S) carries the approximation in S. Group scope only, never mixed with PTD entity figures.

seats.board.share.women from ESRS 2 GOV-1 §21(d) (mandatory regardless of materiality), ratio form from AR 5; counts and board size from the Women on Boards Art. 7 report and national corporate governance reports. Bases differ: ESRS counts every AMSB member including employee representatives and, in two-tier systems, both boards; France's quota leaves out employee-elected directors; Germany's 30% counts the whole Aufsichtsrat. Nivel must choose one board per two-tier company.

Non-executive and executive shares are exact from WoB Art. 7 (seats.board-nonexec.*, seats.board-exec.*), with NL-WIQS and AktG § 96(2) and § 76(3a) for two-tier boards. Committee share only from GRI 405-1-a (voluntary). Chair, CEO, independent directors and committee chairs by gender are not required, though the names appear in governance reports.

headcount.topmgmt.share.women from ESRS S1-9 §66(a) (group; by default two levels below the board, but company-defined, from 14 to 9,745 people across the Euro Stoxx 50). headcount.executives.share.women from France's Rixain declarations (instances dirigeantes, per entity with 1,000+ staff) and Spain's alta dirección rule (LO 2/2024). No executive counts and no KMP; the CEO's gender is not required.

Senior managers: the Rixain cadres dirigeants share (France, per entity). Managers: Spain's EINF employees by sex and professional classification where the company's categories include managers (group), non-managers by subtraction. Italy's art. 46 categories (dirigenti, quadri) are not public. No supervisors level. ESRS covers only top management.

Drops against headcount.all.share.women (ESRS): board (GOV-1 §21(d)), top management (S1-9), executives and senior managers (Rixain), managers (Spain's EINF). Rixain levels are per French entity while E is the group's, so those drops mix scopes unless the entity's own headcount is used. Pay ladder from 2027: an employer's PTD upper-quartile share minus its own E (the mean of its quartile shares).

From 2027 (2026 pay year), per employer: headcount.quartile.share.annual.* and .hourly.* from PTD Art. 9(1)(f), ranking basis set nationally; upper share, spread and men's bands follow. Ireland's GPG gives hourly quartiles per entity since 2022 (market map). Not in ESRS, so there are none at group level for FY2024-FY2025. No band pay levels.

pay.all.gap.annual.median and pay.all.gap.hourly.median from PTD Art. 9(1)(c), per employer from 2027 (Italy: fixed elements only); Ireland's median hourly gap since 2022 (market map). Spain's register medians by sex are not public. ESRS has no median; a few companies give one voluntarily.

The PTD Art. 9(1)(g) basic-pay gap by equal-value category (not public, from 2027) is recorded as pay.all.gap.annual-base.mean with a category qualifier; Spain's register gives mean base salary by sex (not public). The only public figure is GRI 405-2-a's voluntary women-to-men basic salary ratio by category and location, on an unfixed basis. No FTE base gaps; GRI 105-5's basic hourly gap is not yet effective.

Per employer from 2027: pay.all.gap.bonus.mean and .median (PTD Art. 9(1)(b) and (d)) and pay.all.rate.bonus.* (Art. 9(1)(e)); the receipt rates are approximate, since complementary or variable components include allowances and benefits in kind, not only bonuses. Recipients gap = 1 - (1 - per-worker gap) * rate.men / rate.women, approximate because the Directive leaves the 9(1)(b) population open. Ireland's GPG gives recipients' mean and median bonus gaps and bonus and benefits-in-kind receipt per entity since 2022 (market map). No bonus levels.
eu.fixed: The how said 'the receipt ratio is exact', but EU-PTD Art. 3(1)(a) makes complementary or variable components 'any other consideration, cash or in kind', broader than bonus (the research notes 'UK bonus is narrower'). The Irish recipients gaps are now recorded as available.

eu.how: PTD Art. 9(1)(g) basic and variable gaps by category and the Art. 10 joint assessment flag (not public, from 2027); Spain's 25% justification flag (not public); France's pay.all.gap-adjusted.fte inside score.fr-index (public, per entity); company adjusted gaps under ESRS AR 33 (optional, group). Only the French and the optional company figures can be read today.

Concentration: women's share of permanent, temporary and (to FY2026) non-guaranteed-hours staff from ESRS S1-6 §50(b) (group, head count or FTE); full-time and part-time from Germany's § 21 (entity). Gaps: only Ireland's part-time and temporary mean and median hourly gaps per entity (market map). Japan's regular and non-regular split and Australia's casual staff have no EU counterpart.

Spain only: 1 - pay.board.mean.remuneration.women / .men and the executives equivalent from the EINF (group, mean, total pay). pay.all.ratio.highest-to-median from ESRS S1-16 §97(b), which also stands in for the CEO ratio. headcount.top10-earners.count.women from France's Index indicator 5 (entity, under-represented sex). India's median forms and the women's share of disclosed executive pay need individual director pay under SRD II, which is outside the catalogue.

Statutory hires by sex exist only in Italy's art. 46 (entity, not public). Public figures come from GRI 401-1-a (voluntary counts and rates) and the WEPs indicators. Hiring gap = share of hires minus headcount.all.share.women, which mixes a voluntary GRI boundary with the ESRS group. Italy's starting-pay gap (art. 46) is not public.

ESRS gives only flows.all.count.leavers.total and flows.all.rate.leavers.total (S1-6 §50(c); 2026 S1-5 §19(c)). By gender only from GRI 401-1-b (voluntary) and Spain's dismissals by sex (EINF). India's permanent-staff turnover and Australia's resignations are not available.

Promotion counts by sex only in Italy's art. 46 (entity, not public), with rates from those counts over art. 46 headcount. France's Index publishes promotion-rate and raise-rate gaps only as point differences (indicators 3 and 2; missing from the catalogue), so flows.all.rate.raises.* are not available. The WEPs share of promotions is voluntary. No moves into management and no conversions.

Uptake leave.entitled.rate.taken.* from ESRS S1-15 §93(b) (group, FY2024-FY2026, phased in, removed from FY2027); entitlement leave.all.rate.entitled.total from §93(a) and 2026 S1-14 §38. Counts, return and 12-month retention only from GRI 401-3 (voluntary). France's catch-up raise after maternity leave from Index indicator 4 (entity). Japan's new-parent uptake and India's permanent-staff rates are not available.

Only discrimination incidents on all grounds: ESRS S1-17 §103(a) (including harassment) to FY2026, then 2026 S1-16 §42(a) (group). No sexual-harassment count, so India's POSH rate, resolution, backlog and upheld shares cannot be computed. Actions from GRI 406-1-b (voluntary); harassment protocols from Spain's EINF.

Hours ratio from ESRS S1-13 §83(b) and review coverage ratio from §83(a), both by gender for FY2024-FY2026 (phased in) and without gender from FY2027; GRI 404 keeps the split voluntarily. Health and safety and skills training by gender are not available.

Only GRI 202-1's entry-level wage against the minimum wage by gender at significant locations (voluntary, and dropped in GRI 105). ESRS S1-10 adequate wages has no gender split. Minimum-wage counts (India), living-wage shares by gender (GRI 105-4-c, not yet effective) and California pay bands are not available; Belgium's hours by gender per entity are the only hours data.

Only disability: ESRS S1-12 §80 lets a company split the share of employees with disabilities by gender (optional, a percentage, phased in, no split from FY2027). Benefit coverage and union membership by gender are not available; ESRS S1-8 and S1-11 have no gender split.
No EU regime discloses length of service by gender or the retention of hire cohorts.

Board targets from AktG § 111(5) and NL-WIQS (actuals from m.board); executive directors from WoB Art. 5(2); top management from AktG § 76(4) and the Dutch subtop (actuals from ESRS S1-9); France's Index progress objectives below 85 (Index terms, not gap points); company gender targets under ESRS S1-5 (target.other.list); outcome status from HGB § 289f, the SER and WoB Art. 7; board compliance from WoB Art. 7; executive compliance recomputed from Rixain shares and Vorstand counts. Baselines are often missing, so progress is approximate.

Present: equality plan, action plan, pay audit and consultation (Spain's REGCON plans, entity); joint pay assessment (PTD Art. 10, not public); 25% justification and pay records (Spain, not public); harassment protocols and work-life measures (Spain's EINF, narrative); board diversity measures (WoB Art. 7); workforce diversity policy (ESRS S1-1); equality narrative (Germany's § 21); score.fr-index (public). Absent: an equal pay policy flag, carer and domestic violence support, maternity compliance, pay ranges in postings and outsourcing lists; WEPs Tool scores are never disclosed.

CSRD: limited assurance of the whole sustainability statement, so level, provider (named in the assurance report) and scope (every ESRS gender data point) are all given, plus the responsibility statement. In Germany and the Netherlands (CSRD not transposed) the auditor only checks presence and limited assurance is voluntary; Spain's EINF requires independent verification. National regimes (Egapro, § 21, PTD) are not assured.

method.headcount-basis (S1-6 §50(d)), method.gender-basis (the S1-6 categories), method.pay-basis (MDR-M; 2026 AR 34) and method.scope (ESRS 2 BP-1) are disclosed, and headcount.all.count.other comes from the S1-6 table. method.pay-coverage.share comes only from Bloomberg's voluntary framework. Pay basis texts are uneven, so grading each pay gap's elements needs a reading per company.

Group headcount.all.count.total and headcount.national.count.total per country (S1-6 §50(a): countries with 50+ staff and 10% of the total; from FY2027 the ten largest) against national entity headcounts: Germany's § 21 averages (every 3 or 5 years), Belgium's social balance sheet and, from 2027, PTD employer reports (headcount only through quartiles). The ESRS country split is not by gender, so a gender check needs the company's own country tables. ESRS group gaps and PTD or Irish entity gaps never share an index average.

SDG 8.5.1 mean hourly earnings and gap (Eurostat's unadjusted gap is the EU's own version); ILO median, monthly and factor-weighted gaps; the OECD full-time median gap for the 22 EU states in the OECD; SDG 5.5.2 shares of women in management. National statistics, never mixed with company data.

The ethnicity pay gap comes only from WEF's voluntary expanded metric and is rare in the EU, where several states restrict ethnicity data. The board minority share comes from GRI 405-1-a-iii and ESRS GOV-1 'other aspects of diversity' (percentages on company-chosen groups). No disability pay gap.

us.how: No US instrument gives S, pay totals or an all-staff mean gap by gender in public. Route 3, approximate: E from headcount.all.share.women (10-K, voluntary) with W = 1 - pay.all.gap.hourly.mean (WEF SCM, full-time relevant employees) or 1 - pay.all.gap.annual.mean (GRI 405-2-a, per category), on the group; rare, since most US companies publish adjusted ratios instead. Statutory but confidential routes the company already files: Route 2 from the Illinois EPRC wage list (Illinois staff) and Route 3 from California mean hourly rates and headcounts (California staff), both subsets. Never exact: no mean on total pay over all US or group staff exists.

E = headcount.all.count.women / (women + men) from the EEO-1 consolidated report: US payroll staff in one Q4 pay period, binary sex. Exact for the national arm but confidential, public only where the company publishes its EEO-1 (falling; 2024 is likely the last data year). Otherwise public only as a voluntary 10-K share (headcount.all.share.women, registrant-defined, approximate) or GRI 2-7 group counts. No permanent or regular base exists.

W = 1 - pay.all.gap.hourly.mean (WEF SCM, voluntary, full-time relevant employees) or 1 - pay.all.gap.annual.mean (GRI 405-2-a, per category and location, average type unset). Confidential statutory routes: women's over men's California mean hourly rate (W-2 over hours, California staff) or mean annual wages from the Illinois EPRC list (Illinois staff). The usual US figure, an adjusted pay equity ratio (pay.all.gap-adjusted.total), and unadjusted median gaps are not W. Check W against 30-130%.

No rule requires total pay. Approximate as headcount.all.count.total (10-K, basis undefined) times pay.all.median.annual.total (Item 402(u) median employee pay, which understates the mean). Illinois EPRC totals cover Illinois staff only.

P from m.payroll (approximate) and S from m.s (approximate), with E from headcount.all.share.women (voluntary, group). EEO-1 counts would give a national E, but no public national P or S exists, so scopes must be matched on the group.

seats.board.count.women / seats.board.count.total from NY BCL 408 biennial statements (every corporation authorised in New York; sex undefined); Illinois 8.12 self-identified gender for Illinois-HQ companies; otherwise the proxy's named directors (Item 401) with the company's own honorifics, approximate where any director is unresolved. Men by subtraction.

From the proxy roster: positions (Item 401), independence (Item 407(a)), chair and lead independent director (Item 407(h)) and committee membership, with gender only from the company's honorifics. GRI 2-9-c and 405-1-a give composition voluntarily. No US instrument discloses board roles by gender.

Executive officers named under Item 401(b) and named executive officers under Item 402, gender from the company's honorifics; SASB executive management share (voluntary, some industries); top management approximated by the EEO-1 Executive/Senior category (within two reporting levels of the CEO; national, confidential). CEO from Item 401(b).

EEO-1 counts by sex for Executive/Senior and First/Mid-Level Officials and Managers give senior managers, all managers (sum) and non-managers (remainder) exactly for the national arm, on EEO-1 category boundaries; confidential unless the company publishes its EEO-1. Public alternatives: GRI 405-1-b and WEPs shares (voluntary, company-defined levels). No supervisors level.

EEO-1 level shares (national) against the board (entity) and voluntary group shares; scopes and dates differ, so each drop is approximate. Pay ladder only from Bloomberg quartiles (voluntary) or California bands (confidential).

headcount.quartile.share.hourly.women from Bloomberg GEI Q29b-e (voluntary, ranking basis company-chosen); annual quartiles interpolated from California's 12 BLS pay bands (confidential, California staff). No FTE quartiles or band pay levels.

California median hourly rates per job category and race cell (confidential, cannot be combined); medians of the Illinois EPRC wage list (Illinois staff, confidential); a minority of companies publish a global unadjusted median gap under no framework.

pay.all.gap.annual-base.mean from GRI 405-2-a basic salary ratios per category and location (voluntary) or the WEF SCM basic-salary mean gap. No FTE or hourly base pay by gender; GRI 105-5 not in force.
No US rule or framework separates bonus pay or bonus receipt by gender; California and Illinois figures fold bonus into total earnings.

GRI 405-2-a per-category ratios (voluntary); category gaps from California mean hourly rates by job category (confidential); adjusted gaps as the company publishes them (Item 101(c)(2)(ii), Bloomberg Q28). No joint pay assessment, Spain or France items.

Concentration only: temporary and non-guaranteed-hours counts (GRI 2-7-b, voluntary), part-time and intermittent counts (California RY2025, confidential), non-permanent approximated by temporary. No regular-staff split and no pay gaps by contract type.

Director pay (Item 402(k)) and named-executive pay (Item 402(c)) are public by name; gender comes from the company's honorifics, so women's share of disclosed executive pay and board means and medians are approximate (about five executives). CEO pay ratio exact (Item 402(u)); highest-to-median via WEF SCM; manager and non-manager gaps from California job categories. No top-10 earners.

GRI 401-1-a counts by gender (voluntary, group) and WEPs share of hires; GRI rates use a period-end headcount denominator that GRI only recommends. Hiring gap = share of hires minus headcount.all.share.women, which in the US is a registrant-defined 10-K figure, so approximate unless both come from the same GRI boundary. Japan and Italy items absent.
us.fixed: GRI-401-2016 check: the rate denominator is a 'should', not a requirement; and the US headcount.all.share.women (Item 101(c)(2)(ii)) is graded approximate, so a gap against it cannot be exact.

us.how: GRI 401-1-b counts by gender (voluntary, exact where given) and rates by gender, whose period-end headcount denominator GRI only recommends, so the rates are approximate. No permanent-staff rates, resignations or dismissals.
us.fixed: GRI-401-2016 check: 'the period-end headcount used as the rate denominator is a compilation recommendation ("should"), not a requirement'.

us.how: Only women's share of promotions (WEPs EI 6, Bloomberg Q14, voluntary) against headcount.all.share.women; no counts, rates, promotions into management, raises or conversions.

GRI 401-3 gives entitlement, uptake, return and 12-month retention by gender (voluntary, group); entitlement share approximate over GRI 2-7 headcount. No paid-leave weeks, and the Japan, India, Australia and France items are absent.
Only discrimination incidents (GRI 406-1, voluntary; harassment included, no gender split) and a grievance-mechanism flag (WEPs EI 8). No sexual harassment complaint counts, backlog or rate.
Hours ratio from GRI 404-1 and review coverage from GRI 404-3, by gender (voluntary). Skills and health and safety training by gender are not reported.

GRI 202-1 entry-level wage ratios by gender (voluntary, exact where given); California pay band counts and hours by sex (confidential; BLS bands, not tied to the minimum wage). No minimum or living wage headcounts.
No US disclosure of benefit coverage, union membership or disability by gender.
Mean tenure by gender only from Illinois EPRC start dates (confidential, Illinois staff, all staff not indefinite-term, fields unverified). No 10-year retention.

Representation targets only as voluntary objectives (Item 101(c)(2)(ii); Item 407(c)(2)(vi) policy text), many withdrawn after EO 14173; progress against m.board, m.executives, m.managers and m.e. Board compliance from Washington's 25% comply-or-explain rule. No pay-gap, quartile or leave targets.

Mandatory flags or text: pay range in postings (state laws), pay records (California), board diversity narrative (Item 407(c)(2)(vi)), outsourcing providers (California, confidential), pay evaluation statement (Illinois EPRC, confidential). Voluntary: grievance mechanism (WEPs). No equal pay policy flag and no WEPs Tool score: the self-assessment's answers stay with the company. Most flags in the count have no US source.
us.fixed: Follows the change of score.weps-tool and policy.equal-pay.flag to not available (WEPS-TOOL: 'Not public: results are confidential to the company').

us.how: No rule requires assurance of gender figures; GRI 2-5 gives level, provider and scope voluntarily. Signed statements: the Illinois EPRC officer statement and the EEO-1 certification (both confidential); SOX 302 and 906 certify the 10-K as a whole.

Gender basis, headcount basis and scope are fixed by the EEO-1 form (binary sex, one Q4 pay period, US establishments) and pay basis by California's statute (W-2 over hours). The 10-K employee count has no stated basis; pay coverage share only via Bloomberg; headcount.all.count.other only via GRI 2-7.

Group headcount from the 10-K (worldwide, basis and date undefined) against the national arm's EEO-1 total (Q4 US payroll, confidential) and other markets' national filers (UK pay gap employers, WGEA employers). By gender: GRI 2-7 group and regional counts against EEO-1 counts. Dates and bases differ, so checks are approximate; a US group's UK pay gap never enters a US index average.
SDG 8.5.1 and 5.5.2 for the US (ILOSTAT), ILO hourly and monthly mean and median gaps, the 2018/19 factor-weighted gap, and the OECD full-time median wage gap.

Ethnicity pay gap only via WEF SCM (voluntary, not hourly) or California mean hourly rates by race and sex (confidential); minority-ethnic directors from Illinois 8.12 (Illinois-HQ) or voluntary proxy text; no disability pay gap.
